A new key management scheme is presented, in which keys are generated based on relative node location and a non-negative irregular increasing function. Compared to the present schemes, our scheme reduces the consumption of communication and the influence on WSNs security by compromised nodes. Simulation results demonstrate that our scheme is more security and practical.

articleTitle: The Research of Rate Allocation Based on Network Coding in Media Multicast Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Network coding is a new data transmission method which is different from the traditional storage and forwarding routing technology. By using network coding, it can improve the throughput of the media multicast network. This paper study the layer rate allocation optimization problem based on network coding for media multicast network. By optimal allocating layer rate, the total rate of all receiving nodes could be maximized. Because the problem is a nonlinear integer programming problem, so we put forward a heuristic layer rate allocation algorithm. This algorithm decomposes the network graph into child graph by the number of layer according to each receiving node's receiving bandwidth. Thus the minimum value of maximum flow of each receiving node in the child graph is the corresponding layer rate. The results of simulation show that the algorithm can improve network throughput, and the average bandwidth utilization ratio of the receiving node.

articleTitle: A Retransmission Based Collision Solution for Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In cognitive radio (CR) networks, the secondary users are allowed to use the licensed frequency bands of the primary users (PUs) when these bands are vacant. However, once the PUs come back, they may collide with the transmitting secondary users. Therefore, the secondary users are generally required to sense the channel periodically to ensure that the primary users are absent during their data transmission in order to avoid the collisions with primary users. In this paper, we first analyze the performance of the periodic sensing scheme. Then retransmission scheme based on the cooperation of the primary base station(PBS) and secondary access point (AP) associated with Independent Component Analysis (ICA) algorithm is proposed, which relieves the impact of packet loss for primary users, while improving the transmission efficiency for secondary users. The computer simulation shows that under the limited spectrum access chances, the proposed scheme outperforms periodical sensing schemes.

articleTitle: Improvement of Nonrepudiable Threshold Proxy Signature Scheme
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: On the basis of YTH threshold proxy signature scheme, a nonrepudiable scheme with known signers was constructed by Hu et al. in 2009. They claimed that the weaknesses of frame attack, collusion attack and public-key substitute attack can be overcome in their scheme. Whereas this article will demonstrate two security leaks of frame attack and collusion attack inherent in Hu et al.'s threshold proxy signature scheme, which is not as same as they claimed, previously. That is, the original signer can forge a valid threshold proxy signature while the proxy group doesn't know it, and any t or more proxy signers could cooperatively reconstruct the secret polynomial function f(x) to fake a proxy signature. In this article, based on Hu et al.'s scheme, we propose a new and efficient scheme to resist those attacks.

articleTitle: The Throughput Analysis of IEEE 802.11a WLAN with Low-Rate Access Nodes
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The function of multi-rate support (14 rate ranks from 1Mbps to 54Mbps) in PHYs is prescribed in IEEE 802.11 protocol. To analyze the serious affects to the throughput of whole networks caused by the low- rate access nodes, a precise algorithm is proposed based on the improved Markov model in DCF protocol. The throughput of WLAN is conducted with low-rate access nodes, and the simulation results with NS2 prove the conclusion. After that the optimization methods are proposed for the low-rate access nodes, and all these are the effective references for network planning and optimization.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Amplify-and-Forward Cooperative Communication with Adaptive M-QAM Modulation
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper studies the performance of multiple relays amplify-and-forward (AF) cooperative communication system with adaptive M-QAM modulation in Rayleigh fading channel. The average spectral efficiency of the fixed and adaptive rate M-QAM scheme are both researched and analyzed. We come into the conclusion that under certain BER level, the adaptive M-QAM scheme achieves significant efficiency gains over the non-adaptive one. Besides, we obtain the spectral efficiency loss for the fixed rate M-QAM scheme resulting from the increase of the number of the relay nodes which are confirmed can in a great extent be compensated for in the adaptive one. In addition, the simulation of probability of outage for the rate-adaptive M-QAM modulation system exhibits that the adaptive scheme can acquire high successful transmission rate as well as guarantee the bit error rate.

articleTitle: An Antenna Selection Algorithm for TDOA Location Method in Distributed Multi-Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Wireless location has received increasing attention in the last decade, and the introduction of distributed multi-antenna in 4G system has brought in extra information for high accuracy location. In this paper, a novel antenna selection algorithm in distributed multi-antenna system is proposed. By analyzing the least square error of TDOA location method and its relationship with locations of antennas utilized, factors are designed to indicate this relationship, and then we can find the most proper antennas to locate the MS. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna selection algorithm outperforms the traditional methods, which indicates our antenna selection algorithm can be applied in distributed multi-antenna systems effectively.

articleTitle: Cost Analysis of a Novel Mobility Management: Interworking between PMIPv6 and MIPv6
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the cost of a novel mobility management-interworking between Proxy Mobile IPv6 (PMIPv6) and Mobile IPv6 (MIPv6). This paper focuses on scenarios where the two protocols are used by the same mobile node (MN) to manage local and global mobility. In this scenario PMIPv6 is used as a network based local mobility management protocol whereas MIPv6 is used as a global mobility management protocol. We propose an analytic mobility model based on the random walk to take into account various mobility conditions. Based on the analytic models, we formulate the signaling cost, packet delivery cost, tunneling cost, and total cost. Then, we analyze the performance of the interworking mobility management. Simulation results show the validity of the analysis and point out the effect of network environment parameters, such as domain size, session characters and mobile nodes speed.

articleTitle: Research on Co-Channel Interference Analysis Method in UWB Wireless System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The co-channel interference is the most usual interference type of the UWB system, which effects the receive performance of the UWB system. In this paper, a corresponding path loss models based on the propagation feather of the UWB and co-channel interference signals is built, and an analysis method of the UWB co-channel interference based on the co-channel interference guard threshold is presented. Then the co-channel interferences which come from the satellite-based and the earth-based are analyzed profoundly, and co-channel interference rules and calculation methods for interference degree based on the protection threshold are given. It provides the foundation for the analysis of the coexistence between UWB and other communication systems.

articleTitle: Cyclic Spectral Analysis of Costas Signal in Non-Cooperative Receiving
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, inner-pulse parameters model and ambiguity function of Costas signals are built and calculated. The cyclic spectral features extracting algorithm in non-cooperative receiving context are proposed using ACP cyclic spectral estimating method. The normalized RMS error (NRMSE) of Costas signals is measured to verify the validity of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Modulation Technique of High Speed Loran-C Data Channel
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: At the age of global positioning system (GPS), Loran-C is still valuable. Loran-C can be used in the new navigation infrastructure both as a backup navigation and a redundant source of GPS integrity information which is provided by the wide area augmentation system (WAAS). The time information, such as WAAS message, can be added into Loran-C by using Loran-C data modulation. In this paper, several modulation techniques are discussed in detail. To meet WAAS message bandwidth requirements, on the base of Ninth Pulse Communication, we present a new hybrid modulation technique that can significantly increase the data rate of the Loran-C data channel.

articleTitle: An Approach on Wireless Broadcasting Retransmission Using Network Coding
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Considering the disadvantage of traditional “Repeat Request-retransmission” wireless broadcasting transmission, a novel approach to wireless broadcasting retransmission based on network coding is presented. Retransmission information is cached by the broadcast source and lost packets is combined by using network coding for retransmission broadcasting. The correlative theoretical analysis indicated that the retransmission method based on network coding, under the premise of the data solvability of receive node, reduces the number of retransmission. The simulation results show that the proposed approach can improve the throughput efficiency of node compared with HARQ.

articleTitle: The Study of Ultra Wide Band Devices' Synthetic Interference to Third Generation Mobile Phones
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Facing with the scenarios of coexistent of many indoor Ultra Wide Band (UWB) wireless radio devices and mobile telephones, a modified spatial integral model is used to analyze and calculate synthetic Electro Magnetic Interference (EMI) issues of UWB. With Third Generation (3G) mobile phones of CDMA2000, WCDMA and TD-SCDMA chosen as victim receivers, a performance attenuation model of the victim mobile phones is used to calculate the UWB synthetic interference to them. The optimal density of UWB devices and the minimum distance between UWB devices and victim receiver are obtained.

articleTitle: Time-of-Day Analysis of Web User in CDMA Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: CDMA2000 is a family of 3G mobile technology standards, which use CDMA channel access, to send voice, data, and signaling data between mobile phones and cell sites. In this paper, we present some observations of a CDMA mobile network of some city by analyzing the characteristics of the data, such as login time, logout time, delay of transmission, and user attributes. The author provided a basis analysis of regular user behaviors using user attribute pattern clustering. From this observation, the time-of-day behavior gives better indication of mobile user behaviors in CDMA network.

articleTitle: Study on OCNS Application in HSPA+64QAM Field Trial Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Performance verification and evolution is a very important step for some features to implement in the current mobile communication commercial networks. During the period of the field trial for these new features, user equipment is restricted to its development and price. Usually, Orthogonal Channel Noise Simulator (OCNS) is employed to simulate the environment of real network with multiple users. This paper presents the loading principles, power calculation and configuration of OCNS. And some results are given and analyzed for the field trial of HSPA+ 64QAM downlink system based on OCNS method.

articleTitle: Automatic Discovery Techniques for T-MPLS Packet Transport Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: T-MPLS is a connection-oriented packet switched solution for the next generation transport networks. The concept was first proposed by ITU-T in Geneva, Feb 2006. The standardization process is pushed by ITU-T and IETF, many recommendations appeared recently. T-MPLS is much easier to achieve a convergent packet platform for any L2 protocol. It focuses on the packet transport applications that adhere to the standard groups. The OAM, protection and switch function and network management aspects are nearly finished by now but the control plane standardizations have not obtain a common senses about how this technologies evolve in future. In this paper, we compared the automatic discovery requirement in T-MPLS with other discovery techniques used in other network, such as in IP, RPR, Ethernet, ASON, etc. The detail mechanism and protocol in other network are described respectively. As for the intelligent networks, the discovery procedure is done by the control plane due to its responsibilities. Maybe we can use the discovery tools such as SNMP, ARP, ICMP, OSPF, the coordination between the control plane and the discovery process is necessary. Simulation model is also designed in OPNET modular 11.5 to compare these approaches.

articleTitle: A Novel IP Address Auto-Configuration Scheme for MANET with Multiple Gateways
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A mobile node who wants to communicate to the nodes in the Internet must firstly be configured a global IP address. The existing schemes have different drawbacks. A novel IP address auto-configuration scheme for MANET with multiple gateways is presented in this paper. It can provide the mobile node with MANET-local address and global IP addresses and guarantee that these addresses configured by this scheme are unique within the MANET. The proposed scheme can be applied to any scale MANET with lower complexity and lower overhead. Because of the existing of multiple gateways, the mobile node can change one global IP address to another quickly if one is not useable. It supports frequent network partitioning and merging, and can efficiently resolve address conflicts in a timely manner whenever they occur.

articleTitle: A Laser Driver with Analog Pre-Distortion Technique for Radio-over-Fiber System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A 3.3V integrated laser driver with analog predistortion technique for Radio-over-Fiber (RoF) system is presented. This driver circuit is designed in standard CMOS 180 nm technology. The core circuit current consumption is only 15mA. The entire driver circuit works in a band-pass from 1-2GHz as the system specification. Simulated result shows that this circuit works as expected.

articleTitle: Research on the Model of Vulnerability Mining Based on the Local Fuzz
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Fuzz used the concept of black-box testing, is critical to an auto vulnerability mining method, there is blindness in this method. This paper presents a semi-automation model of vulnerability mining based on local fuzz with data stream control and hidden debug technology, the practice shows us that this algorithm makes the fuzz much faster and correct.

articleTitle: A Scalable Privacy-Preserving Protocol for RFID-Based Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Scalability and privacy are crucial for the RFID-based supply chain systems. But few existing protocols consider the scalability requirement and they have security and privacy issues more or less. In this paper, aiming at the special needs of the supply chain, we propose a Lightweight Scalable Privacy-preserving protocol, LSP, which only needs to XOR and hash operations. By introducing the reverse hash chain, LSP greatly reduces the burden on the database comparing with the existing constant-time protocols. Based on our analysis, the protocol can guarantee confidentiality, untraceability, forward security and reader authentication as well as high efficiency. Meanwhile, LSP can prevent desynchronization attack. We also use the MICAz sensor nodes to simulate our protocol and the result shows it spends less time.

articleTitle: Intelligent Academic Communication System Based on an Advanced Software Framework
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: With the spread of a large number of web application, more and more software requirements are proposed. Especially in management information system, it is necessary to maintain the scalability of the database and the flexibility of the software architecture. To meet the development of the software, a lot of novel technologies are presented. The framework based on Struts, Spring and Hibernate is one of the most important. This paper firstly introduces the framework and then gives an application named intelligent academic communication system to explain how the framework works. The result proves the system runs well.

articleTitle: Tracking in Work-in-Process Using a Mobile Terminal Based on MES
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: With the raplid development of manufacturing industry, MES (Manufacturing Execution system) plays an important role within the industry, it can optimize the production process; however, it cannot provide real-time work-in-process during the production. With the advent of a 3G era, workers can scan and decode QR code using a mobile terminal, which is then transferred back to the server through the 3G network. This is an easy process to manage in real-time. Research has shown that tracking products with a mobile terminal based on MES has a wide range of application.

articleTitle: Study on Two Kinds of MGB Evaporation Duct Models
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The propagation path of wireless wave is often affected by many factors. In actual military operations, more and more people have focused on the influence of the air refraction, especially evaporation duct. The reason is that evaporation duct could trap electromagnetic wave, make the path of the wireless wave longer or shorter. At present, an evaporation duct model is still the best tool to evaluate an evaporation duct. In this paper, one kind of evaporation duct models called MGB model is introduced, and we use the experiment data to test the applicability of the two MGB evaporation duct models. The conclusion can offer some help for realizing MGB model.

articleTitle: Personalized Query Expansion Based on an Expert System for Mobile Search
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Compared with the traditional PC-based web search, the mobile search needs more personalization. An approach to personalized query expansion based on an expert system for mobile search is proposed. Our main work concentrates on the algorithms of query expansion. First, environmental information obtained by a mobile device and query terms submitted by a user are formatted into the specific format. Then these treated elements are sent to an expert system to match with the rules. Finally, according to the matched rules, the additional keywords are appended to the query terms so as to catch on the user's search intention. Experimental results shown that the approach we proposed can significantly improve user's experience and has much better performance in precision than that of the existing public search engines.

articleTitle: 3D Face Regulation Based on Surface Deformation
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: 3D face database is an important data platform for model training, algorithm design. Especially for these researches based on statistical learning method, the algorithm performance has a great dependency on training sample set. Subject to the constraint of data acquisition equipment the data structure of current 3D face samples are different. It is incontinent to use these samples without regulation. To solve this problem, this paper presents an regulating method for existing 3D databases based on surface deformation. The experiment results show that the proposed method has good performance on face regulation.

articleTitle: Energy Aware Priority-Based Secure Image Transmission in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Wireless Multimedia Sensor Networks (WMSNs) are gaining research interest due to the availability of low-cost cameras and CMOS image sensors, also due to their broad application opportunities. The energy and resource constrained environment of WMSNs calls for low complexity energy aware image authentication and transmission schemes with minimal overheads. The proposed scheme enhances the data security with stream authentication while minimising the energy utilisation for the authentication as well as transmission by adopting a preferential transmission based on the importance of the data packets in the code stream. Inherent correlation among neighbouring pixels in an image and the multi resolution capability of wavelet coding is exploited to propose an adaptive priority based image authentication and transmission scheme. Simulation results show an encouraging and improved energy efficiency without compromising reconstructed visual quality.

articleTitle: Delaunay-Based Heterogeneous Wireless Sensor Network Deployment
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: For the issue of wireless sensor network deployment in a deterministic monitoring area with obstacles, a low cost heterogeneous sensor network deployment method HSNDelaunay based on Delaunay Triangulation is proposed in this paper. A contour-based deployment is performed to eliminate the coverage blind-points near the boundary of monitoring area and obstacles firstly. Based on the triangulation of the monitoring area, the center of the circumcircle with maximum radius is selected to be the candidate deployment location. The type of sensor with higher coverage and lower waste cost is deployed after the comparison between original sensor and heterogeneous sensor. Experimental result shows that the proposed HSNDelaunay algorithm is efficient in increasing coverage while minimizing the cost.

articleTitle: Research on Video Rendering on Android
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Nowadays there are more and more people using Android related devices. Efficient multimedia players are highly required. Video-audio rendering plays an important role in multimedia players, which is also relates with the platform. It's known to all that Android has many versions, and one app can hardly support all versions. So in this paper, We introduce four methods of video rendering by using JNI(Java Native Interface), and present the process of implementation. Finally, we compare those methods and get a more efficient video-audio rendering way. According to the most efficient rendering way, we will develop android apps for video meeting and surveillance system.

articleTitle: Design of a Practical DSSS Communication System Based on TMS320c5416 DSP
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Direct sequence spread spectrum technology is very important in wireless telecommunication systems and data communication systems because it has many advantages, such as good concealment, and being able to overcome the multiple access interference. A practical DSSS communication system based on TMS320c5416 Digital Signal Processor is designed in the paper, which consists of baseband modulator, IF modulator/demodulator, local oscillator, antenna, Liquid crystal displays monitor and TMS320c5416 DSP, etc. The experiment result of transmission shows that the direct sequence spread spectrum system designed can realize effective data transmission and anti-interference communication with advantages of high data transmission rate and wide spectrum range.

articleTitle: An Effective Spectrum Sensing Method via Space-Time Averaging Technology
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Spectrum sensing is a key technique in the cognitive radio. It enables secondary users to detect spectrum holes and monitor primary users' activity. However, many factors make spectrum sensing much difficult, such as very low signal-to-noise ratio, and noise uncertainty, and quite short sensing time, etc. In this paper, a uniform linear array is configured for each secondary user's receiver. The sample covariance matrix can be effectively modified by the Hermitian and Toeplitz property. Thus, the primary users' signals can be much more accurately detected by comparing the ratio of the maximum eigenvalue to the average of others of the modified sample covariance matrix of received signals with a threshold. Simulation results not only show the proposed method can efficiently overcome the influence of the aforementioned negative factors, but also indicate that it need no knowledge of primary users' signals and noise in advance.

articleTitle: A Service-Oriented Communication System for Heterogeneous Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The diversity of session control protocol, media processing mechanism and channel condition makes it difficult to have universal communication in heterogeneous networks. In this paper we propose a service-oriented communication system which can support different types of services, e.g., session control service, media processing service and network adaptation service. The architecture of the proposed communication system is flexible enough to support a diverse set of users in heterogeneous networks. Experimental results show the superiority of the proposed system compared to the existing monolithic communication systems.

articleTitle: Training Symbol Design for 2-D Least-Squares Channel Estimation
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Underwater acoustic channel is always a 2-D dispersive channel. For 2-D least-squares channel estimation, the design of training symbols is an open problem. In this paper, (i) we derive the optimal relation between the dimensions of the training matrix and the ffective memory lengths of the equivalent discrete-time channel model, and (ii) we propose a simple algorithm for searching suitable training symbols.

articleTitle: A Solution for Increasing Spectrum Efficiency of OFDM-CDMA System with Pilot Tone
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, MISO OFDM-CDMA downlink scheme is proposed as a solution for increasing the spectrum efficiency of the OFDM-CDMA downlink system with pilot tone and threshold detection combining (optimum TDC). The new presented system with MISO included uses space-time block coding applied to two, three and four transmit antennas. BER (Bit Error Rate) performance in the case of Ricean frequency selective fading is evaluated for the original system as well as for the one with MISO included. For that reason an adequate simulation model is developed. The results show that for the same data rate the proposed system with two times less subcarriers, i.e. narrower occupied frequency band provides better BER performance than the OFDM-CDMA system with pilot tone.

articleTitle: Two Different Schemes of Authentication in IEEE 802.16j Multi-Hop Relay Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: IEEE 802.16j Multihop relay network is an important research topic, because it can effectively extend coverage. There are some issues requiring deeply thinking in the multihop relay network. One of the major issues is hop-by-hop authentication of relay nodes. Another issue is the selection of centralized or distributed security architecture. In this paper, we study the two schemes for authentication in multihop relay network in order to explicitly make a choice which security architecture can better achieve our goal.

articleTitle: A Low Complexity Frequency-Domain Parallel Demodulation Structure Combined with Symbol Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A frequency-domain parallel demodulation structure combined with symbol synchronization is proposed by analyzing traditional demodulation structure based on FFT. The structure not only decreases the output data rate of filter to symbol rate but also shortens FFT length, thus the implementation complexity is reduced obviously. In addition, a frequency-domain symbol synchronization algorithm for the improved structure is proposed by illustrating its computational process and implementation architecture. The capture and tracking performance of the algorithm are simulated. The simulation results show that the structure has low implementation complexity and good performance in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environment so that it can meet the practical application requirements in highspeed satellite communication system.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum Generation in Photonic Crystal Fiber with All-Normal Group Velocity Dispersion
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: We demonstrate supercontinuum generation in the telecom C-band in a photonic crystal fiber with all-normal group velocity dispersion. Pumping this fiber with picosecond pulses from a mode-locked semiconductor laser generates a 90 nm bandwidth continuum with typical self-phase-modulation characteristics. Over 1000 optical carriers with uniform precise channel spacing of 10 GHz are generated. In the experiment, the appearance of optical wave breaking is observed, and we provide an analysis of optical wave breaking of picosecond pulses in the photonic crystal fiber.

articleTitle: A 6.25Gbps Adaptive Decision Feedback Equalizer for Serial Data Link in 0.18µm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents a 6.25Gbps adaptive 2-tap decision feedback equalizer (DFE) for serial backplane receiver. The proposed DFE can be used to reduce the effects of inter-symbol interference (ISI) and compensate the loss of the limited bandwidth channel. To meet the high speed requirement, the DFE is constructed in a half rate structure and most of the module such as MUX, adder and D Flip Flop are designed in current mode logic (CML). Additionally, an adaptation engine based on modified LMS algorithm is implemented, including sense amplifiers, a 6-bit up/down counter and a 6-bit DAC. The DFE has been implemented in 0.18 μm CMOS technology and the whole circuit area including pads is 600 × 550 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Post-simulation results show that it can work properly at 6.25bps. The equalized eye opening can be larger than 0.8UI and power consumption is about 21 mW at 1.8 V supply voltage.

articleTitle: Probability-Constrained Robust Beamforming for General-Rank Signal Models
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Adaptive beamformers such as LSMI provide an excellent robustness against various types of mismatches. These beamformers are sometimes too conservative because they are worst-case optimization based beamformers. A rank-one beamformer based on probability-constrained optimization has been proved to have better performance. In this paper, a probability-constrained beamformer for general-rank signal model is developed. The simulations have shown that this beamformer improves the Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ration(SINR) of the system.

articleTitle: On a Cryptographic Key Management Mechanism for Broadband Mobile Dispatching Communications
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient standalone key establishment and management mechanism, which is readily pluggable into any IP based broadband wireless infrastructure for secure multimedia dispatching communications. It is demonstrated via strict security analyses that the solution is not only independently operable off broadband wireless service providers, but also efficient in computation, simple and flexible in applications.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of SC-OVCDM System Based on Shortened BCH Codes
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Shortened BCH Codes are first used in SC-OVCDM system to overcome the disadvantage of higher error floor in a kind of SC-OVCDM systems in this paper, system model and key points of design for proposed system are described, there are two key points in system design: interleaving way and code rate of shortened BCH. Simulations and analysis demonstrate: block interleaver and shortened BCH code with higher code rate can obtain optimal system performance. The proposed system can effectively lower down error floor of SCD-OVCDM system by at least one level.

articleTitle: Design of BICM-ID Systems with Suboptimal Log-MAP Decoding Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper addresses the performance degradation of near-capacity bit-interleaved coded modulation with iterative demapping and decoding (BICM-ID) when both demapping and decoding employ max-log-MAP algorithm. Two approaches are proposed to overcome the performance degradation: scaling of the transferred log-likelihood-ratios (LLRs) between demapping and decoding to mitigate the bias of LLRs values, and decoding-oriented labeling search to avoid the extrinsic information transfer (EXIT) curve mismatch with max-log-MAP algorithm. In addition, balanced labeling search is developed to achieve the EXIT curve-matching over both AWGN and Rayleigh channel. Simulation results have shown that the designed BICM-ID system with max-log-MAP algorithm could be superior to the referenced LDPC-based BICM system in DVB-T2 with log-MAP demapping and SPA decoding, over both AWGN and Rayleigh channel.

articleTitle: An Energy and Link Efficient Clustering Technique for Reliable Routing in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a clustering technique, called ELECT, to provide an energy efficient and reliable routing in wireless sensor networks. The ELECT considers node status and link condition, and introduces a clustering metric, called predicted transmission count (PTX), to evaluate the qualification of nodes for clusterheads and gateways. Each clusterhead or gateway candidate depends on the PTX to derive a priority. The clusterhead or gateway candidate with the highest priority will become the clusterhead or gateway. Simulation results show that the proposed ELECT significantly outperforms the clustering technique using a random selection and considering only link quality and remaining energy in packet delivery ratio and energy consumption.

articleTitle: A Study of TH Precoding System Performance with Imperfect Channel State Information
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: TH (Tomlinson-Harashima) precoding is an important nonlinear precoding method. In this paper, the bit error rate (BER) performance for the TH precoding system is investigated over time varying and dispersive Ricean fading channels. Assuming that there exists a certain delay introduced by the feedback channel, we first model the feedback error of channel station information (CSI) due to the feedback delay. Then the expression of the received signal over the time varying channel is derived. Finally, we analyze the power of interference signal resulting from the delay. Computer simulation shows that BER of the zero-forcing TH precoding system is inverse proportional to Ricean factor, and evident BER threshold occurs when the feedback delay is large.

articleTitle: IR-UWB Received Signal Reconstruction Based on Quantized Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Compressed sensing (CS) theory provides a new solution for low-rate sampling design of IR-UWB receiver, but the quantization process is usually idealized in existent CS based sampling architectures. In this paper, the influence of quantization noise is fully considered, and an IR-UWB signal reconstruction method with high anti-noise performance is proposed. Based on the analysis of the noise distribution characteristics, the signal reconstruction optimization model is revised, and then the performance of Dantzig-Selector (DS) method is compared with the traditional algorithms. Further, a Joint DS-SP method which can self-adaptively select the reconstruction algorithms between DS and SP (Subspace Pursuit) is proposed. Simulation results show that the Joint DS-SP method can not only get the best performance under different noise regions and quantization precisions, but also show a computational complexity trade-off between DS and SP, thus provides a new strategy of CS signal reconstruction for the design of IR-UWB receiver's digital back-end.

articleTitle: A MAC Protocol with Multi-Packet Reception for MIMO Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems are capable of simultaneously capturing more than one packet. Such capability is known as Multi-Packet Reception (MPR), which is new way to improve performance of Ad Hoc Networks. In order to effectively enhance throughput of Ad Hoc Networks, a novel MAC protocol (MIMO-MAC) with MIMO links that takes into account MPR is proposed. It can receive more than one RTS before responding CTS, which maximizes transmission links simultaneously. Receiver determines links according to the number of its own antennas and RTS. Compare to the existing protocol, it allows many communications at the same time in one competitive area. Finally, simulations are implemented in terms of load and source nodes number in OPNET environment, results show that MIMO-MAC outperforms CSMA/CA and CSMA/CA (k).

articleTitle: A Cellular Automata Based Dynamic Load Balancing Algorithm: CAPA
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Though a considerable amount of research has been done on Dynamic Load Balancing (DLB) algorithm and great progress has been made during the last decades, effort in implementing DLB fit for large heterogeneous systems (such as Grid) is lacking. In this paper, a mapping relationship between Global Potential Energy (GPE) and load balancing is obtained by means of hydraulics method and Jenson's inequality. Cellular Automata (CA) is characteristic of concurrent computing and suitable for the simulating of large heterogeneous systems. Making use of concurrency of CA and the theory of communicating vessel in hydraulics,an DLB algorithm-Cellular Automata Programming Algorithm (CAPA) is presented. CAPA transforms DLB problems of large system into the computing of a CA, each cell determines its next state and the quantity of load to be moved based on both the states of its neighbors and its own. Due to the simultaneity and concurrency of CAPA, the balancing speed is quite fast. The simulation experiment demonstrates that CAPA shows great performance when used in large heterogeneous system.

articleTitle: Protocol Analysis and Online Forensics in IPv6 Network Environment
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Although IPv6 protocol has considered and implemented many security mechanisms compared with IPv4, there are still many security threatens in IPv6 Networks. In this paper, we has designed and implemented a network forensics prototype 6Foren in IPv6 environment based on the protocol analysis technology, its functions include packet capture, data reconstruct and messages replay etc. the 6Foren can be used as the online digital forensics which support the online forensic of HTTP, FTP, SMTP and POP3 protocols.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on English-Chinese Bilingual News Document Clustering
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Bilingual or multilingual document clustering is a valuable research. Based on monolingual algorithm, the paper makes a comparative study on monolingual-based clustering and bilingual-based clustering by using the corpus of English-Chinese bilingual news text. The experimental results show that mixed language-based method can make a better and more stable performance.

articleTitle: On the Secret Channel Capacity of MIMO System under Fading Environment
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, the channel capacity of a Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) broadcast system is investigated under correlated fading environment where there exists a transmitter , a legitimate receiver and an eavesdrop, each node equipped with multiple antennas. We derive the secret capacity and its upper bound of the MIMO broadcast channel in detail by using the Information theory and random matrices theory.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Resolve the Dynamic IP Address for the Server-Side Gateway over the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, based on the DDNS (Dynamic Domain Name Service) and port mapping technology, a method about server port mapping and server-side gateway dynamic DNS is introduced, which can be applied in Data Collecting System based on the Internet of Things. In this way, the external sensor-side gateway can access the intranet server which has a dynamic IP address.

articleTitle: A Novel Nonpolarizing Tunable Thin-Film Filter for Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The bandwidth of the S-polarization and the P-polarization modes will separate while the narrowband thin-film filter is in oblique incidence, which will cause serious polarization dependent loss and limit its tunable range. The phenomenon of the polarization bandwidth separation and its relationship to the mirror layers of the thin-film filter are analyzed. One novel method about eliminating the polarization bandwidth separation by optimizing the stack of the filter is presented. According to the stack, a novel nonpolarizing 100GHz DWDM four-cavities angle-tuned narrowband filter is designed. The simulation and the experiment results show that it can eliminate the phenomenon of the polarization bandwidth separation and enlarge the tunable range to cover the whole C-band.

articleTitle: Fair and Stable MAC Scheme to Improve TCP Performance for Wireless Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: It is an undisputed fact that TCP fairness and stability is an important element of a well-designed medium access control (MAC) protocol for wireless ad hoc networks. There isn't a MAC protocol that can fulfil this acquirement although many mechanisms have been proposed in the past. This paper utilizes the collision detection mechanism of the IEEE 802.11 protocol ignored by all researchers to design a novel p-persistent MAC (PMAC) scheme. Our analysis and simulation results have shown that the proposed scheme can perfectly solve the short-term and long-term fairness and stability issues while providing a good aggregate throughput in many topologies. Although the performance of PMAC is dependent on network topology, we provide many methods especially node mobility to effectively improve it. More important, we present a mobility guide by which fair and stable TCP performance can be achieved.

articleTitle: Robust Controller Design for Networked Control Systems with Time-Varying Sampling Periods
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper is concerned with the robust fault tolerant controller design of networked control systems with time-varying sampling periods. Based on Lyapunov stability theory and using LMI approach, new criteria are proposed for the controller design. A numerical example is given to demonstrate the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Identity-Based Secure Multicast Protocol in IPv6
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: To meet the glowing security requirements and multicast demands of internet users, an identity-based secure source specific multicast protocol is proposed for the next generation IFv6 network. The presented cryptographically generated address is improved by making use of the benefit of the identity-based cryptography. So it can not only verify the validity of sender's IF address, but also verify the validity of sender's identity. The security of SSM is improved through the authentication and accesses control of multicast participant. The results of the analysis show that the protocol has high security property, and also has properties of independence on IF multicast infrastructure and favorable scalability.

articleTitle: An Improved Algorithm of Speed Estimation Using Wavelet in LTE
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: To solve the defect of requiring no noise (High SNR) in the algorithm of speed estimation using wavelet, this paper propose an improved local extrema identify method, which can identify the authenticity of local extrema though the amplitudes between them. The simulation based on several speed scenarios of LTE shows the performance of improved algorithm is much better than that of the original algorithm in high, medium, and low speed, respectively.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization for Cooperative Spectrum Sensing in Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Spectrum sensing is a fundamental requirement in cognitive radio (CR) networks. When the constraint on detection performance is satisfied, the achievable throughput of the CR networks is expected to be maximized. Considering from a basic frame structure of CR networks, both the sensing time and the number of CRs have effect on the throughput. Current research on maximizing the throughput focuses on assuming that one parameter is fixed and coping with another one. As a result, the throughput is maximized in terms of only one factor. To overcome this drawback, a joint optimization scheme to maximize the throughput is proposed in this paper which chooses both the sensing time and the number of CRs as the optimization parameters. The optimization problem is formulated based on a throughput model with constraint on giving adequate protection to the primary user and it can be solved by an iterative algorithm. Simulation results are provided to show that significant improvement in the throughput of the CR networks has been achieved by using the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A Two-Party Identity-Based Key Agreement Protocol with Explicit Authentication
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A two-message two-party key agreement protocol with explicit authentication provides perfect forward secrecy. Digital signatures can usually be used as providing explicit authentication for a key agreement protocol. Shim proposed an efficient identity-based signature scheme using bilinear pairings; however, he did not give a formal security proof for it. In this paper, we present a formal security proof for Shim's signature scheme. Using Shim's signature scheme as building blocks, we propose a new two-party identity-based key agreement protocol with explicit authentication. The proposed protocol satisfies a set of desirable security properties. Compared with the related protocols, the proposed protocol has distinct advantages in terms of security and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: A Method for Obtaining Constant Envelope Quadrature Modulation System Base-Band Signal
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this article a new method based on the function sin<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>(πt/2T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>) is proposed to obtain 2T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>-long base-band signal which can be applied to quadrature modulation to make the modulated signal constant-enveloped and phase-continuous. The power spectrum of the signal attenuates more quickly and the out-of-band radiation decreases. The general expression of the signal is given and the time-frequency property has been analyzed. We established the modulation-demodulation model and realized the modulation and demodulation process by using MATLAB. Bit error rate characteristic has been analyzed and the simulation results proved the validity of this method.

articleTitle: Tail Data Iteration in SC-FDE without CP System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents the influence on performance in SC-FDE (Single Carrier with Frequency Domain Equalization) without CP (cyclic prefix) system. ICI (Inter Carrier Interference) is imposed since channel respond not appear circular. To alleviate the interference, we propose a simple method by using the tail data in the frame to compensate. But error is also introduced. In order to reduce it, iteration is taken into account. Simulation results show that the combination of tail data and iteration has a low complexity but a performance similar to that with CP.

articleTitle: A Compact Construction for Nonbinary LDPC Codes Using Permutation Polynomials
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A compact construction for nonbinary low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes over GF(q) (q>2) using permutation polynomials (PPs) is proposed in this paper. Following the previous compact construction for binary LDPC codes using quadratic permutation polynomials (QPPs) over integer rings, a QPP whose coefficients are chosen for maximizing the girth is used for determining all the positions of nonzero elements in the parity check matrix of a regular nonbinary LDPC code. Moreover, it is proposed to use a linear permutation polynomial (LPP) over GF(q) for determining the distribution of nonzero elements of GF(q) at the nonzero positions. Computer simulation results of LDPC codes over GF(8) have shown that the propose compact construction can attain similar error correction performance with Mackay's random construction for nonbinary LDPC codes.

articleTitle: A Cross-Layer Design Based on Link Quality for Cognitive Wireless Mesh Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: To resolve channel interference and “Deafness” problem in cognitive wireless mesh network, a new Cross-layer Design based on Link Quality for Cognitive Wireless Mesh Networks is proposed. When the node chooses the channel, it is not only in accordance with the rank of channels, but also based on link quality. In this way, cross-layer technology can be effectively achieved, and network performance can be improved. Simulation results show that compared to the link-based channel allocation algorithm, capacity and interference based channel allocation algorithm, and channel diversity based channel allocation algorithm, the new CLDLQ algorithm has an obvious advantage in the performance of delay and throughput.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based QoS Guarantee Study of Wireless Multimedia Communication
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: QoS guarantee in wireless multimedia communications is a major difficulty, this paper introduces cloud technologies to ensure QoS in wireless multimedia communications. First introduced the characteristics of cloud computing technology, and research QoS guarantee in wireless multimedia communications system architecture, detailed analysis the modular of multimedia coding algorithm, adaptive control techniques and error resilience technology. Wireless multimedia communications security control technology is studied.

articleTitle: Expected Density of Progress of Cognitive Radio Networks with Selection Region Based Routing Protocol
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Cognitive Radio networks which consist of primary and secondary networks are widely considered efficient systems to solve the serious problem of spectrum scarcity. The data transmission of secondary network is subject to the spectrum opportunity provided by primary network. In this paper, we investigate expected density of progress of secondary network with three routing strategies which are farthest receiver, random receiver and nearest receiver rooting strategies based on selection region. Numerical results show that the best performance can be achieved with nearest receiver routing strategy, and a maximum of expected density of progress could be got by setting an optimal transmission probability with that routing strategy.

articleTitle: Flexible Frame Design for Carrier Aggregation Device in IMT-Advanced System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In IMT-Advanced system, carrier aggregation makes use of continuous or non-continuous spectrum which may be scattered in many channels, and then the individual component carrier frame is combined to form a new frame structure named frame aggregation. In this paper, flexible frame aggregation strategies are designed for different carrier aggregation situation in order to reduce the duplex delay existed in time division duplex (TDD) mode. The flexible frame aggregation not only supports backward compatibility and asymmetric business but also improves the efficiency of hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) and channel quality information (CQI) feedback process.

articleTitle: The Algorithm of Coverage Base on Probability Sensing Model in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper analyzes the existing algorithms of coverage of WSN, then proposes an algorithm of coverage of network base on the probability sensing model. First, the algorithm judges whether exists a sponsor set of the node i where node i is any node in the monitoring area. If the sponsor set is not existed, the node must keep working; else the algorithm executes the next steps. Determine whether the node would go to sleep taking into the probability of networks. The simulation results show that the agreement reduces the number of working nodes, extends the network's life cycle effectively, and achieve the desired network coverage.

articleTitle: Design of the OFDM Signal Generator Based on ADS and FPGA Simulation
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Based on the IEEE 802.11a protocol, ADS software was used to simulate the OFDM signal wave and system spectrum ,data rate ranging from 6 to 54 Mbps. Then a 24Mpbs rate OFDM signal generator was designed based on the FPGA simulation ,and the simulation results were analyzed and compared. Xilinx Spartan-3E was selected as the FPGA platform and Verilog HDL language was used in programming the FPGA chip. The results of the design were fine in the process of debug in the Modelism environment.

articleTitle: Robust Semi-Blind Channel Estimation for MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Proposed is a novel Orthogonal Procrustes (OP) based semi-blind channel estimation method for multi-input, multi-output (MIMO) systems. The main idea of our technique is, using specific properties of the OP algorithm, to estimate the optimum rotation matrix from channel matrix instead of to estimate channel parameters directly. This results in substantially improved estimation accuracy. Furthermore, the introduced semi-blind scheme is shown to be very efficient when the number of the receive antennas is no less than the number of transmit antennas. Analytical expressions for the mean-square error (MSE) of the proposed algorithm are derived in closed forms. Various numerical examples show that our proposed algorithm can achieve the much better estimation accuracy than the existing LS technique.

articleTitle: An Improved Dynamic Spectrum Access Protocol Based on the Greedy Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In cognitive radio networks, media access control protocol decides the method how the nodes in the networks receive and send data by shared wireless channels. Whether the MAC protocol can use the limited channel effectively plays a very important role in the performance of the cognitive radio network. Focusing on designing and implementation an excellent MAC protocol in cognitive radio networks, this paper describes an improved dynamic spectrum access protocol based on the greedy algorithm. The simulation results shows it's good performance.

articleTitle: Load Balance and Discovery of Multi-Agency in Mobile Video Grid
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper studies some issues to implement multi-agency in Mobile video grid, the load balance among the mobile agents used by one mobile synchronously; the discovery of multiple agents for one service and the requirement for network topology. After analyze in theory, a series of simulation experiments in NS-2 are carried out to verify the theoretic conclusions. The results show it can benefit by implementing multi-agency in mobile video grid.

articleTitle: Web Services Selection with User Security Attributes Preferences
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Along with the rapid development of Web services, user always want to make select decision according to their special preference demands of security attributes. This paper address the problem of service selection based on the Web services security assessment. First we use questionnaire to obtain the semantic and fuzzy information of user security attributes preferences. And then language fuzzy scale is been used to get the user's preference weights of security attributes. In the following, several sorted and assessed optional services can be used to provide intuitive and effective decision-making basis for services selection. Finally we present a detailed design and demonstrate the effectiveness of our Web service selection process through experiment result.

articleTitle: A Movement Control Strategy Based on Virtual Repulsion and Aggregation Algorithm in Multi-Tier Mobile Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) is the hot research topic. In order to adapt to the future development direction of WSN, this paper presented a movement control strategy based on virtual repulsion in Multi-tier Mobile Sensor Network. The strategy first used a hierarchical node aggregation algorithm to divide all sensor nodes into many communication clusters in the monitoring area. It combines virtual repulsive force to distribute nodes uniformity in every cluster. Finally, using aggregation algorithm again based on the nodes uniform distribution to design fusion nodes' optimal movement route for data collection. The simulation results show that the strategy can ensure the efficiency of network data collection, reduce data loss rate, and nodes power consumption.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Power Control Scheme Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Although power control has been explored since 1990s, there still remains the need for further research. Since the optimization objectives always contradict each other, we propose a scheme which solves the power control problems by combining a multi-objective technology with a genetic algorithm. The proposed algorithm can realize the optimal control of power in a CDMA system. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can decrease the total transmission power consumption significantly with a low outage percentage. The system capacity is therefore increased.

articleTitle: Quaternary Golay Complementary Sequences Derived from Binary Golay Complementary Sequences
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Golay complementary sequences play quite an important role in communication and radar. In this paper, we present a family of quaternary Golay complementary sequences. The resultant sequences result from conversion of the existing binary Golay sequences, and both have the same length and number of subsequences. Our method can provide rich quaternary Golay complementary sequences due to a large number of binary Golay complementary sequences available.

articleTitle: A Data Delivery Approach Based on Location and Velocity Vector for Delay Tolerant Mobile Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Delay Tolerant Mobile Sensor Networks (DTMSN) has the enormous potential to expand its applications in many previously impossible fields. Because of its intermittent link and limited network resources, this network needs an effective data forwarding algorithm to ensure valid data forwarding and highly delivery ratio. Recent approaches have drawbacks of computing nodes' delivery probability, because they only paid attention to partial factors. In this paper, a Location and Velocity vector based data Delivery approach (LVD) was proposed, which gives an in-depth description of nodes' motion state, and more accurately calculates the delivery probability based on the location and velocity vector. Simulation results show that this approach cannot only improve the message delivery rate with lower transmission overhead, but also reduce data transmission delay.

articleTitle: Rate Maximizing with Adaptive Bit Partition in Cooperative Distributed Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In multi-user cooperative distributed antenna system (DAS) with limited feedback, multi- user interference (MUI) within the service cell and inter-cell interference (ICI) from adjacent cells are inevitable because of the quantization error. Considering this, we propose an adaptive bit partition scheme,which allocates more bits to quantize the stronger interference channels and changes with channel conditions. Based on our derived upper-bound of average data rate loss, the simulation results show that the proposed scheme has at least 0.5~1dB rate improvement than other average-bit partition schemes, especially in high signal to noise ratio (SNR) region.

articleTitle: Optimal Relay Location for Asymmetric Fading Channels in the Cellular Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Relay system attracts increasing research attention for Multihop Wireless Network, and then RSs location is a vital optimization variable to richly exploit the advantages of adopting RSs. In this paper, we aim to resolve the optimal location of RSs in a two-hop network to maximize system capacity. We first derived a tight close-form approximation of ergodic capacity and outage probability over the asymmetric fading channel with interference in the three-terminal relay system. After that the expression of system capacity is obtained. Lastly, the Monte-Carlo simulations and numerical analyses are performed to evaluate the performance to acquire the optimal location of RSs.

articleTitle: A Novel Reconfigurable Planning for Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Proposed by Joseph Mitola III in 1999, Cognitive Radio (CR) has been considered as a promising solution for intelligent and efficient utilization of scarce spectrum in the communication world. CR brings about flexibility and self-adaptability to networks, by deploying most of functions on software. As the future communication era enables efficient utilization of radio resource, shrewd management of network elements, and dynamic adjustment to the environment, CR will surely play an influential role. This paper depicts a reconfigurable approach for end-to-end performance evaluation in Cognitive Radio Networks (CRNs). Based on Progressive Theory (PT) that derives from Complex Network Theory (CNT), the proposed approach caters for an extensive content of reconfigurability and performance-complexity tradeoff. The reconfigurable method explores the end-to-end performance in a rigorous manner, and takes all the Network Elements (NEs) of end-to-end transmission links into account. In addition, an end-to-end performance engine depending on cognitive cycle and classification tactic is demonstrated in detail. The classification tactic grades the evaluation factors in a novel way with a range of diversity sets. At last, a concise conclusion is put forward.

articleTitle: Signaling Analysis of Iub Interface in TD-SCDMA
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Signaling is the premise of communication. Signaling analysis is an effective means of network optimization, and it has many applications in the 3G communications. TD-SCDMA specially services for the 3G communications of China. With the research and development of TD, its versatility and scalability draw the world's attention. Yet the analysis of TD-SCDMA in Iub interface is rare. This paper deeply studies the signaling analysis method of the Iub interface protocol stack of TD-SCDMA, which has been verified valid in the experiment.

IEEE Keywords: Time division synchronous code division multiple access

articleTitle: Visual Measuring Image Compression Based on Listless SPIHT Encoding and the Best Wavelet Packet Tree Structure
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents a novel method of visual measuring image compression based on wavelet packet decomposition. Firstly, the high frequency sub-band decomposed by the wavelet transform is further decomposed into multiple directional sub-bands, so as to present the edge of the image more sparsely and accurately. Secondly select the best wavelet packet tree structure through comparing cost function among sub-bands, which is in compliance with the feature of visual measuring image. Thirdly in order to protect almost all detailed information, high-frequency was be emphasized according to the standard deviation of every sub-band. Last but not least, combined listless SPIHT encoding not only save memory space but also could be implemented by hardware conveniently. The experimental result shows that the novel compression method of visual measuring image has better capability of compression and maintaining accuracy.

articleTitle: Location Management and Optimization Research of 3G Network for High-Speed Railway
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The article begins with the particularity of the 3G user in high-speed railway, then divides the user terminals into different groups according to the regularity of the movement, and takes the method of appropriate location management to save the overhead of paging. Oriented paging is used for the stationary user, tracking paging is used for the regularity mobile user, and queued packet paging is used for the irregularity mobile user, all of above approach is adopted to improve the efficiency of location management.

articleTitle: Comparison between Single Mesh Network and Cell Based Mesh Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Industrial wireless applications have stringent requirements of safety, data update rate, time delay, reliability, failure tolerance, and security. In this paper, a concept of cell-based mesh networks is proposed, and the performance is evaluated by computer simulations. The results show that the average number of hops from sensor nodes to the backbone routers and the average route cost are significantly reduced with a comparison to a conventional mesh topology in multipath fading environments. It is also shown that the cell-based mesh networks can tolerate failures of links, notes and backbone routers. All those imply that the cell-based mesh networks are suitable for industrial wireless sensor networks with stringent requirements of data update rate, time delay, and reliability and failure tolerance.

articleTitle: Computing the Average Symbol Error Probability of MPSK System with Receiver Imperfections
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The average symbol error performance of coherent detection of M-ary phase-shift keying (MPSK) signals with receiver imperfections is analyzed for the Rician and Rayleigh fading channels in this paper. Considering phase error, quadrature error, and I-Q gain mismatch, closed-form expressions for the average symbol error rate (SER) are derived. Our new theoretical expressions can offer an effective evaluation of the average SER for an MPSK system with various cases of receiver imperfections both in the Rician and Rayleigh fading channels.

articleTitle: Optimal Wideband Spectrum Sensing Using Iterative Second-Order Cone Programming
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Spectrum sensing is an essential functionality that enables cognitive radios (CR) to detect spectral holes and to opportunistically use under-utilized frequency bands without causing severe interference to primary users (PU). The state of art for wideband spectrum sensing is given by Multiband Joint Detection (MJD). Constraints on utilization and interference have to be imposed to solve the optimization problem. Unfortunately-because of the nonlinearity of constraints, the optimization problem may not solved efficiently. In this paper, a method based on second-order cone programming (SOCP) is proposed to solve the optimization problem, in which highly nonlinear constraints are approximated through second order Taylor expansion, and successfully incorporated into a SOCP framework. Simulations are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Routing Strategy at Intersections in Vehicular Ad Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: VANET (Vehicular Ad Hoc Network) is a special case about MANET(Mobile Ad Hoc Network), has also received extensive attention as a part of ITS (Intelligent Transportation System). Although it is a promising technology, due to different kinds of factors (such as high speed, particularity of road, traffic system, etc), the routing technology becomes the important challenging problem in Vehicle Ad Hoc Network. We assume each vehicle is equipped with a short range wireless communication device, as is a controller node placed in every intersection with data forwarding system. This paper sets up a mobility model at intersection and present mathematical analysis by the use of Markov analysis method, then proposes a novel routing strategy and shows the performance of the proposed scheme is better than the traditional flood one by simulation.

articleTitle: The Constant Code-Rate Algorithm Research on Encoding Multiplexing Based on MPEG-2
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: MPEG-2 encoding multiplexer is the core for transmission in the digital TV system, owning to all programs, data and different value-added services are transmitted after packaged and multiplexed. Currently, only a few companies outside master the core algorithm technology and ensure that high quality images are transmitted. However, the imported equipment is extremely expensive and the algorithm is more complex, it can not guarantee that a simple implementation of hardware and software. This article uses a simple algorithm and completes the elementary Stream (ES) multiplexed into transport stream (TS).It describes the technology background of transport stream multiplexing, analyses the existing technology based on MPEG-2, discusses the methods for ES multiplexed to TS ,and especially involves one research to constant code-rate control based on TS multiplexing.

articleTitle: A Novel Semi-Static Inter-Cell Interference Coordination Scheme for Cellular OFDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a novel semi-static inter-cell interference coordination scheme based on spectrum pool is proposed for cellular OFDMA systems. In the proposed scheme, the spectrum is divided into three partitions, called major subbands group, minor subbands group and spectrum pool group. The major subbands and the spectrum pool are used by all users in a cell and the minor subbands only can be used by cell center users. The proposed scheme consists of two stages, i.e. at the frequency planning stage, the eNB allocates the major subbands and the spectrum pool to cell edge users and the minor subbands to the cell center users according to variation of the cell edge traffic load; at the intra-cell scheduling stage, the cell edge users are scheduled based on the major subbands and the spectrum pool first, and then the cell center users are scheduled on the remaining resources. The proposed scheme not only enhances the cell edge throughput but also reduces the inter-cell signaling overhead and complexity. Simulation results and performance analysis validate the effectiveness and good performance of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: An Objective Quality Assessment of Multimedia Service Based on Cross-Layer Optimal Mapping
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In order to provide the end-to-end service with QoS support, a novel objective quality assessment adopting the cross-layer optimized mapping from the key components' value of application layer to the subjective score of user-layer is presented in this paper. In this framework, the maximum likelihood estimation to the subjective score in subjective quality assessment with lower complexity is presented at first to avoid the complexity of the least-squares estimation.
