Then the optimal selection of the key component based on the highest loading is obtained, which take out the correlation among the application-layer parameters and simple the mapping form the key component to the application-layer equipment. At last, an optimal multiple regression line mapping based on the maximum likelihood decision is presented, which utilize the statistical quantifying outcomes of the subject score and adjust the coefficient of the mapping according to the fluctuation of those outcomes. This optimal mapping avoid the un-accuracy resulted from the ignorance of the statistics of the subjective score in the liner dynamic curve fitting. The objective quality assessment in this paper is facile to online monitor by the subject score or quality assess based on network scene. The computation and the simulation show that our suggestion outperforms the old one.

articleTitle: Adaptive Power Allocation with Relay Selection for Decode-and-Forward Relay System Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we consider a dual-hop wireless multirelay system with decode-and-forward (DF) cooperative protocol. Assuming the knowledge of channel gain magnitudes, we explore adaptive power allocation based on genetic algorithm with a simple opportunistic relay selection strategy to minimize the system outage probability under an aggregate power constraint. Simulation results show that the presented optimal power allocation significantly enhances system performance. Moreover, it is also found that more candidate relays will decrease system outage probability even the relays do not actively transmit.

articleTitle: Managing the Mobility of a Cooperative Ad Hoc Network Using Clusters Formation and Potential Function
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A cooperative ad hoc network is a collection of wireless devices that collaborate with each other to form a network system that dynamically adapts to changes in an unknown environment to achieve a given goal. Such a network is often built from mobile devices. Mobility modeling is a critical element that influences the performance characteristics of an ad hoc network. In this paper, we describe an algorithm for calculating mobility patterns for mobile devices that is based on a cluster formation and an artificial potential function. Finally, we present the application of our mobility model to simulation-based design of a self-organizing and cooperative ad hoc network.

articleTitle: A New Joint Diagonalization Algorithm with Application to Blind Source Separation
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a novel iterative algorithm for the joint diagonalization of a set of real symmetric matrices is presented. The approximate joint diagonalization of a set of matrices is an important approach in many blind source separations (BSS) applications. By applying the least-squares criterion, a classical nonlinear least-squares cost-function of the BSS problem is obtained. An explicit method for optimizing the cost function is derived and compared with other techniques in the BSS context. Both simplicity and efficiency were achieved by applying the algorithm to BSS problems.

articleTitle: A Decentralized Fusion Architecture Based on Geodetic Coordinate System for Naval Ships Cooperative Engagement
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Considering the design of data fusion architecture for naval ships cooperative engagement in wide sea battleground, first, the cooperative engagement information flow are analyzed from the technical and combat point of view. In addition, the advantage and disadvantage in different coordinate system are discussed in detail. According to the scientifically analyzed result, a decentralized fusion architecture based on geodetic coordinate system for naval ships was presented according to the concept of Network-Centric Warfare. To verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed fusion architecture, a simulation testbed is developed. The proposed architecture is applicable to the over-the-horizon cooperative engagement in the modern naval battle. It can effectively unify tracking and fusion algorithms in short range, intermediate range and long-distance circumstances and simplify the process of system information calculation, which also can provide the system with merits of scalability, robustness, modularity, adaptivity, and self-organization.

articleTitle: Complexity-Constrained H.264 Video Coding in Wireless Environment
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Nowadays, real-time video applications on portable devices became more and more popular. In this paper, we propose a novel joint computation-rate-distortion optimization algorithm for H.264/AVC-based wireless video communications through handheld devices under power constraint. Firstly, we propose a computation resources (CR) allocation model, which is based on virtual computation resources buffer (VCB) and employs the previous method for computation consumption quantitative measurement to facilitate the optimal allocation of constrained CR for each frame. Secondly, in order to meet the allocated CR, we develop an encoder based on complexity adjustable motion estimation (ME) and inter mode decision (MD). The proposed algorithm takes end-to-end distortion into consideration to address the distortion caused by packet loss. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can minimize the end-to-end distortion in the environments with both packet loss and power constraint.

articleTitle: The Design of Low Noise Amplifier Based on MGA-665P8 for RFID Reader
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper studies and analyzes the low noise amplifier applied for 2.4GHz RFID reader fused MGA-665P8. The design introduces low noise amplifier's circuit structure and the principle of work. In the circuit, the schematic simulation and co-simulation are offered to obtain the S parameter and noise figure and two types of results have a comparison. It is confirmed that the results can be in good with the difference with the actual circuit. Finally the text proposes some measures to improve the disadvantages.

articleTitle: The Error-Correction of AAL2 in ATM System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The AAL2 of ATM switching system uses the cyclic redundancy check code(CRC) to correct one bit error of the Common Part Sub-layer payload head(CPS-PH). Heavily based on CRC principle, in this paper analyses the process of one bit error correction of the CPS-PH is explored in detail.

articleTitle: Simulation for Hierarchical Structure and Distributed Radar Netting
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Network distributed radar track fusion with hierarchical structure is enhanced for distributed data fusion, it has its own characteristic and difficult. In this paper, a two hierarchical structure based fusion frame is describe, simulation plat base on HLA is proposed, the component and framework is described, the process and realization during the whole fusion course for low -lever and high lever fusion center is analyzed, finally the demonstrated simulation is shown.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Network Selection Scheme in 4G Composite Radio Environments
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The next generation wireless communication network is expected as a composite radio environment including multiple Radio Access Technologies. Therefore, how to select an optimal network for subscriber to achieve Always Best Connected in this heterogeneous network environment is becoming a popular research field. In this paper, an adaptive network selection scheme is proposed. The Cobb-Douglas utility function in microeconomics is introduced to measure subscriber's satisfaction to different networks, which considers both user preference and QoS criterions. In order to test the performance of proposed scheme, two scenarios are proposed and the simulation results are given at last.

articleTitle: A New Method for Communication Traffic Prediction and Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a new method based on Auto Regressive(AR) model is proposed to predict the communication traffic data and detect if the traffic data is anomaly. The method includes four phases: extraction of traffic data characteristics, data analysis and model determination,determination of model parameters, traffic prediction and anomaly detection. With the simulation, it is obvious that our method can predict future traffic data with high consistency. Moreover, the computational complexity of our algorithm is acceptable for real work.

articleTitle: A Novel Audio Watermarking Algorithm Based on Chirp Signal and Discrete Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Audio watermarking is a hot research area in copyright protection of multimedia content. In this paper, a novel watermarking technique is proposed based on discrete wavelet transform and chirp signal. The special spectrum distribution characteristic of chirp signal is utilized to encode watermarking bit. Then we use radon transform to decode the embedding information. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has good perceptual quality and robustness performance on various attacks such as signal processing and MPEG compression. The ease of use and low complexity reveals our method has good prospect in real application.

articleTitle: Research and Simulation on MBOC Modulated Navigational Signal
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Multiplexed Binary Offset Carrier(MBOC) Modulation signal is a novel form of satellite navigational signal which is recommended by GALILEO for its E1 OS signal. And it is also adopted by GPS for its L1C signal.This paper describes the definition of MBOC and represents its power spectral density.Autocorrelation function of MBOC is also explained.After compared with BOC(1,1),it is obvious that MBOC occupies more advantages in multipath and tracking performance.Then, according to the mechanism of MBOC,a simulation model based on Simulink is set up,which will deepen the understanding of MBOC.

articleTitle: A Novel Wireless Sensor Network Architecture for Crowd Disaster Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Disasters aroused due to dynamic movement of large, uncontrollable crowds are ever increasing. The inherent realtime dynamics of crowd need to be tightly monitored and alerted to avoid such disasters. Most of the existing crowd monitoring systems is difficult to deploy, maintain, and dependent on single component failure. This research work proposes novel network architecture based on the key technologies of wireless sensor network and mobile computing for the effective prediction of causes of crowd disaster particularly stampedes in the crowd and thereby alerting the crowd controlling station to take appropriate actions in time. In the current implemented version of the proposed architecture, the smart phones act as wireless sensor nodes to estimate the probability of occurrence of stampede using data fusion and analysis of embedded sensors such as tri-axial accelerometers, gyroscopes, GPS, light sensors etc. The implementation of the proposed architecture in smart phones provides light weight, easy to deploy, context aware wireless services for effective crowd disaster mitigation.

articleTitle: The Interference Constrained Pilot Design for NC-OFDM Systems in Cognitive Radios
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The pilot design is one of key issues for non-continuous orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (NC-OFDM) systems in cognitive radios. A new design of the optimal pilot position and power allocation under a interference temperature constraint has been presented in this paper, the presented scheme minimizes the mean-square error(MSE) of the least squares(LS) channel estimate under a primary user(PU) interference temperature limit. Simulation results show that the PU interference temperature constraint can change the optimal pilot positions and power distribution.

articleTitle: Distributed Rate Allocation Algorithms in the Emergency Communication over Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the video stream distributed transmission problem for the emergency communication over heterogeneous wireless networks. The key issue of the transmission problem is how to guarantee the quality of service, when the video stream is transmitted by multiple wireless access networks. According to observed available bit rate (ABR) and round trip time (RTT) over each access network, we propose four distributed rate allocation algorithms with different optimization objectives, in term of the average packet loss rate, the maximum delay, the proportional fairness and the benefit fairness of networks. Simulation results show that these four proposed algorithms can perform well both in fairness and effectiveness. Furthermore, the video distortion minimization algorithm and the maximum delay minimization algorithm tend to be more practical since the video quality is important in the emergency communication.

articleTitle: Path over in Mobility Multihoming Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: MSCTP is an important scheme for implementing end node mobility with transport layer in mobility multihoming network, how to improve the performance of mSCTP to further support a large scale real-time multimedia transmission is the focus of this paper. So we modify mSCTP by adding QoS-Measurement-Chunk used for path-over process in mobility multihoming networks. In this paper, Congestion-oriented Path-over Algorithm (CPA) was proposed to detect congestion existing in the primary path. The simulations show that CPA is more robust to adapt change of the wireless link parameters and the performance of suggested method is batter than mSCTP.

articleTitle: ML-Decoder and Criterion of Designing Codebook for a Relay Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: For a relay network system with amplify and forward (AF) protocol, in this paper, analysis of performance is conducted and an upper bound of pair-wise error probability is obtained under assumptions that (i) relays only forward received signals (do not perform signal processing), (ii) the receiver only knows Channel State Information (CSI) from relays to the receiver, (iii) the transmitter and relays do not have any CSI. Based on this upper bound, a criterion of designing codebook is proposed. Surprisedly, this bound also shows that increasing number of relays can hardly improve performance, and furthermore, the error probability is decreasing with a speed of P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, no matter how large the relay's number is, where P is the total energy. These results are all confirmed by simulations.

articleTitle: Dual Layer Beamforming with Reduced Channel State Information in TD-LTE System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Time division duplex long term evolution (TD-LTE) system specified by the 3rd Partnership Project (3GPP) supports beamforming which can fully exploit channel reciprocity. And spatial mulplexing such as dual layer based beamforming has been supported on release 9 of the 3GPP specification in recent years. The performance of beamforming utilizing channel reciprocity depends on the accuracy of the channel state obtained by the base station (BS). The critical factor in this respect is the density of the sounding reference signal (SRS) transmitted from the terminal. Moreover terminals are not required to support sounding from all receiving antennas so this behavior is supposed to impact the dual-layer beamforming performance heavily. In this paper we investigate the impact on the performance of average and coverage throughput from practical sounding limitations and the evaluation results show that performance losses are negligible in most cases. For the special case of dual layer transmission with single antenna sounding we propose two beamforming schemes, all of which utilize the combination of long-term beamformer and inter-stream orthogonality criteria (but different criteria for the two schemes) to maximize performance. The simulation results show that the proposed schemes could guarantee the dual-layer beamforming performance even in case of very sparse sounding resource.

articleTitle: Cooperative Spectrum Sensing Algorithm Based Database Decision
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Cooperative spectrum sensing can improve sensing capability of the system. But in a system which owns channels of different protection levels, it will bring bad effects to detection performance when using a single sensing algorithm and data fusing rule in different channels of this system. Therefore this paper proposes a cooperative sensing algorithm, which is based on policy database to select different measures for various channels by diverse protection levels. The performance of this algorithm is simulated in the model of Okumura. The result shows that the proposed algorithm of policy database has better detection performance when compared with the method of one single sensing algorithm and fusing rule.

articleTitle: Research of Sphere Decoding Detection Algorithm in LTE-A System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) has become a popular technique to increase spectral efficient. Meanwhile, the design of cost-effective receiver for LTE-A system remains a challenging task. The sphere detection algorithm performs exact Maximum Likelihood (ML) detection algorithm, however, its decoding complexity is greatly impacted by the initial radius of decoding. A new type of sphere decoding algorithm based on threshold is proposed in this paper. This new algorithm, considering the influence of signal-to-noise ratio and channel condition number on detection algorithm, has lower sphere decoding complexity and ensures performance of sphere decoding. This algorithm has been applied to the LTE-TDD wireless integrated test instrument and has shown perfect performance.

articleTitle: A Randomness-Based Evaluation Method for Spreading Codes of GPS Signal
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The evaluation method is the basic tool for satellite navigation systems' spreading codes design and performance analysis. This paper schemes a novel randomness-based evaluation method for spreading codes. Five basic randomness tests and the significance level are proposed in the scheme. The spreading codes of GPS L2C/L5/L1C signals are evaluated with the method. The result shows that the randomness affect the correlation and security of spreading codes, and the randomnessbased evaluation method is helpful for designing the signal structure of satellite navigation systems.

articleTitle: Statistic Properties of Highway Systems in Wireless Networks: A Random Line Process Viewpoint
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In the paper of M. Franceschetti's, they prove there existing a considerable number of open paths in wireless networks, called highway system. Their theoretical analysis shows the highway system is the key to the efficient operation of wireless networks. This paper established a line process model for the highway systems of wireless networks, and investigate the statistic properties of highway systems, including the estimation of deployment density and the expected number of highway crossing, i.e. highway router. The results of this paper are of practical value for performance optimization of mobile networks and give a deeper understanding of the fundamental properties of highway systems in wireless networks.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a New Compressed Differential Frequency Hopping System in AWGN
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new Compressed Differential Frequency Hopping(C-DFH) system over traditional Differential Frequency Hopping(DFH) system. In the receiver part of DFH system, it needs to detect all the possible frequencies in the bandwidth, which makes the spectrum resource become the technological bottleneck of DFH. However, the proposed C-DFH system can compress the bandwidth of spectrum by using non-orthogonal signals. The performance analysis in Additive White Gaussian Noise(AWGN) is given with the corresponding numerical results and simulation. All these prove that the performance of the C-DFH system is better than the traditional DFH system in the same bandwidth.

articleTitle: An Ant Colony Dynamic Route Guidance Algorithm of Multi-Route Searching Based on Immune Genetics
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper proposes an algorithm combining the Immune Genetic Algorithm (IGA) with the Ant Colony System Algorithm (ACSA) in order to optimize the travelers' route choices in the process of traffic route guidance.It mainly takes advantage of the dynamism, positive feedback and distributed computing nature of the ACSA, and at the same time compatible with the global searching capability of the IGA and easy to combine with other algorithms. And to improve the evolving speed, this paper proposes a Multi-Route Searching Based on Ant Colony System Algorithm (MRSBACSA). This algorithm is capable of speeding up the convergence, meeting the needs of traffic dynamic changes and satisfying travelers. In the eil51 problem, simulation results indicate that our algorithm worked out a better solution comparing with other algorithms. While simulating real traffic conditions under the MapX environment and looking for an optimal path using our algorithm, simulation results indicate that this proposed algorithm can find a route that meets the travelers' needs in the real road conditions.

articleTitle: A Novel Cooperative Layered Video Multicast Scheme
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Multicast is a spectrum-efficient way to support emerging multimedia services over wireless network, where a group of users receive messages over a common wireless channel. Cooperative transmission is a promising technology to improve multicast performance by exploring the cooperative diversity. Different from conventional cooperative multicast schemes, we take the heterogeneity of the multicast group users into consideration and propose a novel two-stage cooperative scheme to accommodate different users with different video quality flexibly. Video streams are coded into base and enhancement layers using scalable video coding technology. The users that successfully decode base layer in stage 1 can receive enhancement layer from BS in stage 2, while the users with bad channel conditions only decode base layer with the help of fixed relays during two stages. The simulation results show that compared to previous multicast schemes, the proposed one can help the users with good channel quality achieve a better spectral efficiency performance while guarantee all users can receive basic video services. We also analyze the the impact of power allocation in stage 2 on the spectral efficiency of both layers.

articleTitle: A Generic Engine for Recognizing Scene Categories
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Because the trade-off between discriminative power and invariance varies from task to task, no single kind of feature is optimal in all situations. In this paper we build a generic scene recognition engine based on multiple cues which capture the different characteristics of the images. Our method can be equally applicable to a range of tasks including scene and object category recognition tasks. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on a large, challenging dataset of fifteen natural scene categories.

articleTitle: Research on LDPC Coding Scheme for Relay Cooperative Communication
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This article analyses the Frame Error Rate (FER) performance with the Pairwise Error Probability (PEP) and presents a LDPC coding scheme for Relay Cooperative Communication (RCC) system. In this scheme, the Degree Distribution of excellent LDPC codes is considered and the LDPC check Matrix is divided into several sub-blocks with different mean column weight (MCW), then specific sub-blocks are transmitted in different transmission Modes. In the Broadcasting (BC) Mode, the sub-block with large MCW has high priority to be transmitted by the source node to make sure the relay nodes correctly receive and re-transmit the signal, which can obtain the system diversity gain. In the Multi-address (MAC) Mode, the source node and relay nodes transmit sub-blocks that haven't been used before to form the complementary redundancy structure in the terminal node, and earn high coding gain. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of this coding scheme for RCC system.

articleTitle: A Retransmission Scheme of Wireless Link Layer for Improving TCP Performance
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: An improved scheme mARQ of link layer selective retransfer is proposed to elevate the TCP performance in the wireless circumstance. This schema sets a limitation to the sum of retransfer times on the basis of the characteristic, that is, each data packet can be divided into several wireless frames ,so that the retransfer time of a frame can be allocated adaptively according to the requirement. The simulation of the system shows that compared with traditional one, the new designed scheme can obtain a larger throughput at a lower error packet rate in the circumstance of high error frame rate, consequently improves the performance of wireless TCP.

articleTitle: The Uplink Power Control Algorithm of the Femtocell System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The introduction of femtocells brings more interference to cellular system, setting threshold to femtocell users' transmit power can control it effectively. To control the interference from femtocell users to macro base station and guarantee the QOS and maximize system capacity, this paper develops the uplink power control algorithm of femtocell system based on threshold and water- filling theorem. The initial value of transmit power is determined according to the interference suffered by macro base station. The simulation results show that the algorithm maximizes system capacity on the basis of interference control.

articleTitle: Statistical Tests for Signal Detection Using Random Matrix Theory
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Signal detection is a fundamental problem in cognitive radio. Energy detection is optimal for detecting independent and identically distributed (iid) signals, but not optimal for detecting the correlated signals. This paper introduces a unified framework for the signal detection where the noise variance and the channel between the source and sensor are unknown at the receiver. The statistical tests are proposed based on the sample covariance matrix calculated from the received signal samples. Using the recent results from random matrix theory, a practical way to evaluate the threshold for the tests is provided. Statistical tests do not need any information of the signal, the channel and noise power as a priori. The Performance of the statistical tests are compared with energy detection (ED) algorithm and covariance absolute value (CAV) method through simulation analysis. Simulations based on voice recorded signals are presented to verify the proposed statistical tests.

articleTitle: Study on NGN Development Business Safe Mode
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Based on NGN present security current situation, set up the security frame of NGN. Open the characteristic of network business to NGN, put forward NGN safe demand model. This model and UML technology combine together, constructs the security mechanism of NGN in terms of different business effectively.

articleTitle: An Anti-Jamming Technique Based on Correlated Pre-Windowing Filter in DFH Receivers
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The DFH (Differential Frequency Hopping) technology brings high performances for HF (Frequency Hopping) communication systems. Symbol-by-symbol detection has been widely used in DFH systems, but the anti-jamming (AJ) performance is poor. In order to achieve better AJ performance, a novel anti-jamming technique based on Correlation Pre-Windowing Filter (CPWF) on frequency domain is proposed in this paper. The technique is performed on the basis of the frequency transition function (FTF), and all of the wideband receiving frequencies can be limited to several frequencies which may be used in the next Frequency hopping. Meanwhile, the symbol error propagation can be eliminated by combing prewindowing filter and comb filter. The symbol error rate (SER) of the DFH receiver with the technique is simulated and analyzed over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels. The results show that the DFH receiver with the technique can improve the AJ ability and enhance SER performance over AWGN channels effectively. Simultaneously, the receiver complexity is reduced significantly due to DFH signal processing on frequency domain. Hence the Anti-jamming Technique will be of great value to engineering applications.

articleTitle: Moving Weak Targets Detection Using an ARMA-Based Bioinspired Model
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The extraction of useful motion information in clutter scenes is a challenging task. In this paper a bioinspired model based ARMA filters was adopted to detect the moving targets. The model took advantage of the facts that insects are capable of discriminating the moving targets in clutter scenes. It used the photoreceptor stage and the larger monopolar cells (LMCs) stage to improve the performance of the elementary motion detection model. The photoreceptor stage increased the contrast between the targets and background to make the weak moving targets more salient. Then spatiotemporal high-pass filters in LMCs stage removed redundancy in space and time domain, meanwhile highlighted edges of targets and areas of relative movement. The simulation results indicated that the ARMA-based bioinspired model detected the weak moving targets robustly in clutter scenes.

articleTitle: Mutual Interference Avoidance and Modulation Mode in OFDM-Based Cognitive Radio System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the relation of Mutual Interference Avoidance and Modulation Mode that aims at maximizing the capacity in OFDM-based opportunity spectrum access(OSA) systems. The continue phase modulation techniques for OFDM systems are considered.We try to decrease the mutual interference between the SUs channel and license frequencies. We show that the traditional PSK modulation with raised cosine filtering applied in general OFDM systems emit much radiation to license bands due to the subcarrier power leak in such systems. A mutual interference avoidance method based on OFDM-CPM is proposed and show better performance .

articleTitle: Effective Fine Timing Synchronization Based on Pilot Resolution and MDS Estimation for a Coherent DRM Receiver
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Receiver timing synchronization is one of the most important tasks in DRM system. An effective method of fine timing for DRM is presented. Firstly, it is shown that characteristics of DRM pilot pattern from consecutive OFDM symbols can increase the resolution in time and frequency domain to obtain exact channel impulse response (CIR). Secondly, we take Maximum Difference Scaling (MDS) which arrived the best fine timing point during the input samples in DRM receiver to get the concentration of the CIR. This approach has no path "alias" and is always able to synchronize to the first arriving path even though it is not the strongest path. In the actual coherent DRM System, this method proves to be effective and reliable.

articleTitle: Efficient Object Segmentation Using Background Estimation for H.264 Video
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: H.264 is an up-to-date video coding standard with wide applications. In order to improve the segmentation efficiency for H.264 video, a novel object segmentation approach using background estimation is proposed in this paper. Firstly the preprocessing including spatiotemporal filtering and motion field accumulation is used to remove the noisy motion vectors and obtain the dense motion field. Then the inter-frame coding modes are applied to estimate the background region, which can reduce the processing time for the subsequent global motion compensation. Finally depending on the residual motion field, the hypothesis testing is exploited to distinguish between moving object region and background region. Experimental results for several video sequences demonstrate high processing speed and good segmentation quality. The proposed approach can effectively extract the objects from H.264 video by using the estimated background.

articleTitle: Research on Performance Simulation of Streaming Media Based on the Wireless Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The wireless mobile network is a dynamic environment. The characteristics of the wireless mobile communication include limited channel bandwidth, high BER, dynamic change over time, unstable channel quality, mobile node, competition of multiple users to share the channel, and the users' wireless signal interference from other nodes of the shared channel. These characteristics of wireless communication make us face a serious challenge to provide QoS guarantee of real-time streaming media application in the wireless network environment. In this paper, the NS emulation method is used to study the performance of MPEG-4 streaming media in the IEEE802.11 g wireless local area network environment.

articleTitle: Incentive Compatible Power Control in Wireless Networks: A Mechanism Design Method
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Power control plays an important role in the design and optimization of a wireless system. In this paper, we use mechanism design theory to model the problem how a base station with limited power allocates power to each mobile user. An optimal mechanism is proposed which satisfies incentive compatibility constraint and individual rationality constraint. After some manipulations of the constraint conditions, we can simplify this complex mechanism design problem to a more simple maximization problem. Then we show this simpler maximization problem can be reduced to a relaxed optimization problem which is a convex optimization problem that can be solved efficiently and exactly using interior point methods or some other methods. Through solving this relaxed optimization problem, an optimal mechanism is proposed. We also prove that the optimal mechanism solved by relaxed optimization problem also is an optimal mechanism of the original optimization problem. The developed mechanism can make the base station's revenue maximization.

articleTitle: Topology Control Protocol Based on Cell for Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Topology control is an important research direction in wireless sensor networks. Due to the huge number of nodes in wireless sensor networks and the irregular distribution of a wide range, it is difficult for a centralized control. In this paper, research about topology control is carried out. In order to reduce the energy loss of the clustering algorithm in cluster head selection process, this paper proposes a clustering topology control algorithm. In the case of a known location information, a clustering algorithm based on cell division is used. The algorithm is characterized by low communication and computation cost, can play a balanced of energy and prolong the network lifetime, and to facilitate the role of data integration. It can achieve a certain degree of network reconfiguration .

articleTitle: Study of Synchronization Techniques Based on TDT for Ultra-Wideband Wireless Communication System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Timing acquisition (STBC) is one of the main challenges in the field of the ultra-wideband communication. "Dirty template" (timing with a dirty template, TDT) timing acquisition algorithm is perfectly suitable for ultra wideband (UWB) technology. In the mode of data auxiliary (DA), it has the characteristics of low complexity and the rapid acquisition. But, in auxiliary (NDA) mode with no data, the performance depends on the random signal interference by the system. Therefore, this paper analyzes the possibility of solving the problem by the orthogonal Hermite pulse method. The calculation uses a string of alternate orthogonal Hermite pulse to send the signal, and modifies original TDT algorithm to realize the synchronization. This method doesn't require the training sequence, Our approach shows a good performance in NDA mode. Consequently, the algorithm performs better compared to the original TDT in terms of the mean square error (MSE).

articleTitle: Periodic Radio Variability of Unevenly Sampled Time Series: Weighted Wavelet Z-Transform Analysis
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The observation of period radio variability in astronomical systems provides astronomers with valuable information on the physical nature of the system. However, because of poor weather conditions and complex underlying astrophysical processes, the data sets of astronomical fields always feature sparse and unevenly spaced sampling. In this paper, a search for periodicity has been presented using the Weighted Wavelet Z-transform (WWZ) technique of the radio light curves of the high mass X-ray binary EXO 2030+375, the weighted wavelet Z-transform (WWZ) technique which is based on the principle of wavelet analysis can detect the characteristic parameter of the time series which the data is unevenly spaced. Periodicity analysis using two other transform methods, Lomb-Scargle periodogram (LS) and Phase Disoersion Minimization (PDM), served for verification and comparison, the results from the three methods are in excellent agreement and identify one persistent periods of ~0.3 (7 hours) day, it provides a reasonable method for characteristic parameter extraction of unevenly spaced time series.

articleTitle: Automatic Target Recognition Based on Discrete Wavelet Transform and Principal Component Analysis
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents a method for automatic target recognition based on discrete wavelet transform (DWT). This proposed method is firstly detecting regions of interest in the original image and then selecting the three-level lowest frequency subimage of each region as the feature vector. To reinforce the performance, principle component analysis (PCA) is incorporated for dimensionality reduction of feature vectors. During classification, nearest feature space (NFS) classifier are presented for robust recognition in presence of varying viewpoints, illumination, and expression. Experiment results show that this proposed method achieves a significant improvement in automatic target recognition rate with high dimension reduction of the feature vector.

articleTitle: New Algorithms of Cooperative Sensing and Recognition of Signals in Cognitive Radio
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In order to solve recognition of modulation signals, which is an important issue in cognitive radio, the paper proposes a new algorithm of recognition of modulation signals. The paper firstly analyzes a new algorithm of cooperative sensing and simulates it in low SNR. Secondly, it proposes new expressions of transient characteristic parameters and shows the procedure of how to define the thresholds. Finally, this paper shows and analyzes the simulation results. The simulation results show that the new algorithm of cooperative sensing has good detection performance. The transient characteristic parameters proposed in the paper have strong anti-noise ability and they can be as robust signatures.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Mode BPF Using Cascaded Square-Loop Resonators for TD-LTE Application
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel dual-mode bandpass microstrip filter using cascaded square loop resonators for TD-LTE application is presented. It is composed of two square rings and designed at the operating frequency of 2595 MHz with a bandwidth of 50 MHz. The rejection performance is improved due to the introducing of cascade method in dual-mode filter design.

articleTitle: Emergency Managing and Scheduling Platform with Electronic Image Hotspot Map
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In order to assure the high efficiency and accuracy of dealing with emergency incidents, it's the essential factor of dispatching the materials and human resource in time. Electronic image hotspot map can visually present the status of resources scheduling in different areas. AJAX engine can make a bridge between client side and server side. Furthermore, it makes the separation of web-page and application. In our paper, two data response strategies which not only drop the load of client side and server side but also greatly shorten the response time are proposed for optimizing the response efficiency in the process of clients' asynchronous requests. Experiments suggest that the designed emergency managing and scheduling platform with electronic image hotspot map by using AJAX can dynamically monitor the real-time data of scheduling resources and make the submitted serious faults effectively show in electronic image hotspot map. Meanwhile, the scheme based on data response strategies could further make the program's performance better.

articleTitle: Research on the Security Issues and Counter Measures of Wireless Mesh Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Wireless mesh network is a new technology of wireless networks, and its properties include self-organization, self-repairing, multi-hop and point-to-point. At the same time, wireless mesh network brings new security questions and challenges, for example, the security routing. This paper presents the security issues and counter measures of wireless mesh network, which include Route Security, Location Information Security, Security Authentication and Security Architecture.

articleTitle: Design Consideration for LTE Channel Estimator Implementation with Greedy Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The greedy algorithms are efficient ways in reconstructing the sparse signal. Among all the greedy recovery algorithms for practical compressive sampling(CS), Subspace Pursuit(SP) can offer reliable recovery accuracy with low costs. In this paper, the SP algorithm is optimized by reducing the complexity of the least square(LS) calculation in each iteration. The Optimized SP performs well in LTE channel estimation when compared with the other greedy algorithms. The utilization of Partial Fourier Matrix helps reduce the matrix storage in SP hardware implementation. The matrix inverse calculation is also simplified by taking advantage of the Hermite Toeplitz matrix generated from the Fourier Matrix.

articleTitle: An Echo Measurement Method for Wireless Repeater with ICS Function
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: It is always a big problem in wireless repeater that isolation is not enough. As the receiving antennas receive useful signals from base station, it also receives interference signals from repeater's transmitting antennas. If the isolation is lesser than the gain of a radio repeater, it will result in the repeater going into feedback oscillation. Based on debugging isolation as the technical background, an echo measurement method for wireless repeater is presented. Firstly, using CAZAC codes as the means for channel initial estimation secondly use variable step size LMS arithmetic to track the channel exactly. The result of test which uses DVB-T signals as the source proves the effect achieved by this function.

articleTitle: A Scheme of Carrier Synchronization Used in the High Dynamic Environment
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The paper proposes a scheme of carrier synchronization in the large rate-of-change of Doppler frequency and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) communication environment. The scheme has two mainly parts: capture and tracking. In the capture part, it utilizes Discrete Fourier Transformation (DFT) and Quinn algorithm to estimate the initial frequency offset. In the tracking part, Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) is used to estimate carrier parameters when the SNR is low, and the Kalman filter is used to track parameter changes. The results show that the scheme can be used in the high dynamic communication system with low SNR.

articleTitle: Interactive RFID Based Driver Assistance and Safety Warning System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: As the transport accidents remain one of the principal causes of mortality in our modern life, various accident prevent mechanisms are proposed to pre-detect the violations and pre-notify the accidents. However, these conventional mechanisms or solutions require either exact recognition or complex algorithms or real-time updating of digital map. In this paper, a RFID-based driver assistance and safety warning system is proposed to automatically detect various traffic violations and warn the drivers to avoid accidents. Indication flags are written in the RFID tag to indicate the various events. The interaction between the roadside and vehicle RFID systems dynamically initialize and release these indication flags to automatically detect and notify the driver of traffic violations.

articleTitle: A Slot-Wise LMMSE Estimate Algorithm for Frame Slotted Aloha Protocol of RFID System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Frame Length Aloha (FSA) is a popular anti-collision protocol in Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) system for its simple and efficient. A major factor which effects the performance of FSA greatly is the estimation of tag population. In this paper, we propose a Slot-Wise tag estimator which can estimate the tag population slot-by-slot and its closed form is derived. Simulations show that the error of proposed tag estimator is less than the existing ones especially when the number of slot observed is small. The proposed estimate can be used in in-frame adjustment scheme to efficiently improve the throughput of the FSA system.

articleTitle: Trusted Vertical Handoff Algorithms in Mutihop-Enabled Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The integration of various networks which adopt different wireless access technology can improve wireless transmission performance and provide mobile users with always best connection. Vertical handoff is the foundation of the integration of the heterogeneous wireless network. In the process of vertical handoff, handoff algorithm is an important part, directly determining handoff performance. Considering the current research hotspot Ad hoc network, multihop is able to expand coverage area of network and reduce single-hop transmission distance. Therefore, a multihop-enabled vertical handoff algorithm TVHOA with multi-attribute is designed in this paper and trust management mechanism when multihop is established to improve the handoff performance of mobile nodes and the network performance after handoff. The simulation result indicates: the algorithm proposed in this paper is superior to traditional SSF (strong-signal first) in the aspect of handoff times, handoff time and throughput.

articleTitle: Augmentation-Based Topology Control Algorithm for Space Information Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In the view of the large scale and increasing kinds of service of space information networks, a service- oriented topology control algorithm is proposed. According to demands of existing service, the topology of network is divided into several logical sub-topologies, on which construct the corresponding topology. Taking the communication pattern as an example, the augmentation-based approach is adopted to construct topologies which can meet the requirements of one-to-many communication. The augmentation-based approach calculates the weight of links, according to the requirements of service on bandwidth, delay, delay jitter and reliability. After that, the augmentation-based approach use the free links as most as possible, establish a nearest neighbor graph that meets the requirement of fault tolerance, then augment to be the ultimate topology. The simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm can remove redundant links effectively, improve the effectiveness of data transmission and also ensure the fault tolerance of the network, can adapt to the multiple application requirement of space information networks.

articleTitle: PIR-Writing Protocol That Supports Information Share
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The rapid development of the Internet and the progress of network facilities, cloud database services are very popular with the web users, which allows users to retrieve, update and delete the records of the cloud database. However, these users of such services do not always trust the cloud storage provider to keep their privacy. Therefore, neither the user's database information nor the access pattern is revealed to the storage server. PIR-Writing can protect the user's update privacy from the storage server. In this paper, we propose a new PIR-Writing scheme which support cloud database information sharing by multiple users. Especially, our protocol keep the communication cost o(logn) which is lowest until now. Further more, it can improve the computation cost of PIR-Writing from o(nlogn+ln) to o(1). Meantime, our scheme has a good availability and security.

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Power Digital Baseband Controller for Passive UHF RFID Tag
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel low-power digital baseband controller for Ultra High Frequency (UHF) passive Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tag is presented in this paper. By analyzing the system design, it is carefully divided into several modules, and it also adopts some advanced low power techniques for system design, based on Electronic Product Code (EPC) Class-1 Generation-2 (C1G2) UHF RFID protocol. The Pulse-interval encoding (PIE) decoder uses a novel double-edge-triggered counter to reduce a half of clock working frequency, then the power dissipation of the system can be reduced evidently by selecting the low-power CMOS cell and dividing the system clock to get the scatter backscatter link frequency (BLF). The chip was fabricated in Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC) 0.18μm standard CMOS process, and the final power consumption is 13.1μW. Test results show that it can support the basic command for the tag selection, inventory and the access.

articleTitle: Research on Wireless Mesh Routers Development for Broadband Internet Access
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Wireless Mesh Networks (WMNs) can be used to provide broadband wireless Internet access through Internet Gateways, the inherited selfishness problem from multi-hop ad hoc network is attracting more and more attention from many researches. As wireless mesh routers may belong to different network operators, in the aim to provide sufficient Internet throughput to its clients or avoid traffic congestion, a selfish mesh router fully or partially drops the relay packets originating from other mesh routers. In this paper a game theory and network coding based design of mesh routers deployment is proposed to solve this mesh routers selfishness behavior. Theoretical analysis and extensive simulations can show how our algorithm (TDNC) can increase the network throughput in the presence of selfish mesh routers and better ameliorate network performance compare to oblivious routing for WMNs and shortest path routing without any incentive.

articleTitle: Interference Assessment in Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: As one of dynamic access technologies, cognitive radio technology is a promising technology to improve the frequency efficiency by allowing the cognitive radio nodes to use the under-utilized spectrum which is not used by the primary users with the spectrum sensing ability. However, because of the imperfectness of the sensing algorithms and the time-varying wireless channel effects, such as shadow fading and multipath fading, the detection performance of the secondary users maybe decreased, and resulting in interference to the active primary users. In this paper, we propose a new systematic interference assessment theory and methodology in cognitive radio networks, including assessment process, assessment index, and assessment methods, intensifying the knowledge and research of this subject which has not been given adequate attention.

articleTitle: Investigation on Spatial Reuse by Using Virtual Relay in 60GHz Dense Environment
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The directivity characteristic in 60GHz communication brings great potential to do spatial reuse in a dense environment, which usually requires the ability of network to support concurrent connections within the same space. This paper proposed a new approach to achieve interference mitigation and spatial reuse, which use the physical reflector as the virtual relay to forward signal to the target node. The exhaust method is used to perform path selection to maximize the overall channel capacity. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the overall channel capacity can be improved and the outage ratio of link can be decreased.

articleTitle: Two Efficient Algorithms Based on Majority-Logic and Min-Sum Algorithms for LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Recently, an iterative soft information reliability-based majority-logic (ISRB-MLG) decoding algorithm was proposed for Euclidean geometry LDPC (EG-LDPC) and Projective geometry LDPC (PG-LDPC) codes. This paper first presents an iterative soft information reliability-based min-sum (ISRB-MS) decoding algorithm based on ISRB-MLG and traditional min-sum decoding algorithm. The performance of ISRB-MS algorithm is greatly improved with a little more complexity than ISRB-MLG algorithm, it mainly needs integer additions and logical operations. Different from traditional min-sum decoding algorithm, the extrinsic information transfer of ISRB-MS algorithm is simplified, we use the full information that all check nodes pass rather than the extrinsic information to update the bit nodes information. Then a modified iterative soft information reliability-based min-sum (MISRB-MS) decoding algorithm is proposed. Compared to (ISRB-MS) algorithm, MISRB-MS algorithm multiplies a scaling factor, so it needs some extra multiplication, but it achieves better performance. Simulation results show that the two algorithms achieve excellent performance and fast convergence rate, they only needs about 10 iterations, if an appropriate scaling factor is chosen, the performance of MISRB-MS algorithm very closes to that of sum-product algorithm (SPA).

articleTitle: A Case Study on Access Control Rules Design and Implementation of Firewall
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: With the rapid development of firewall technology, access control rules design has become one of the most important tasks for firewall technologies. In this paper, the TopSec's network guardian is adopted to design access control lists, and a configuration case for a typical enterprise network environment based on source and destination IP address is given.

articleTitle: Promising Low Noise Amplifiers Using 90nm CMOSFET Devices
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: The wide availability of LNA components varying from 6.0 GHz to 30.0 GHz is delivered using TSMC 90nm CMOS processes. The voltage gains are substantially improved and the noise figures are noticeably reduced. In addition to the multiplication of gains, the multiple stages of amplifiers give the benefits of taking control of noise figures (NF) and approaches to the one of the pre-amplifier. Even though NF gets higher for higher RF frequencies, the suppression of minimum noise figures is to be observed.

articleTitle: On the Performance of Two Cells Systems with Adaptive Beamforming and Delay Feedback
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, the influence of feedback channel delay on system throughput of the cooperative multi-cell system with adaptive beamforming selection is discussed. On the one hand, multi-cell cooperative processing (MCP) has the potential to boost spectral efficiency and improve fairness among users. However, the traditional centralized multi-cell cooperative scheme, where a central processing unit is assumed with the global knowledge of all the required downlink channels and user messages to jointly design BSs, incurs significant overhead and complexity, and will hinder the practical implementation of MCP. We adopt the decentralized cooperative scheme with adaptive linear pre-processing transmission. The objective of the scheduling is to maximize the total system throughput. On the other hand, transmit beamforming as a simple yet efficient technique can exploit the benefits of multiple transmit antennas provided that the instantaneous channel state information (CSI) is known at both sides of transmission link. In order to have such improvements, the CSI at both link ends must be updated timely. However, the updating process is always subject to non-ideality such as feedback delay and estimation error, which destroy the performance. The performance of proposed scheme in terms of the average throughput per cell. The multiuser diversity gain is also investigate throughput simulation. Simulation results show that The performance of a multicell cooperative transmission strategy is highly dependent on the quality of the CSI.

articleTitle: A Novel Method of Topology Modeling in Heterogeneous Wireless Network
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In the future network research, network simulation and modeling is very important. If the topology model of network is not consistent with the actual network, the conclusion is not correct. Heterogeneous wireless network has characteristic of Hierarchy, Power law distribution, Self-similarity, Rich-club property and others. Based on the actual network topology model analysis and using complex network theory, we put forward a topology modeling method suitable for heterogeneous wireless network. Simulation result shows that the proposed method works well, and has more realistic characteristics of the heterogeneous wireless network.

articleTitle: Multilevel Cross-Layer Feedback Based Adaptive Video Coding for Wireless Transmission
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, a multilevel cross-layer feedback based adaptive video coding scheme is proposed to enhance the robustness of the wireless video transmission. Two level cross-layer feedbacks are developed in this work to achieve timely and accurate channel-aware: one is the feedback from physical (PHY) to applying (APP) layer, named PHY-APP feedback, which is used to get the available bandwidth of the physical channel using the feedback mechanism of adaptive modulation and coding (AMC); The second one is the feedback from data link (DL) layer to APP layer: an agent is deployed at the DL layer to predict the possible frame losses by analyzing the DL layer's automatic repeat request (ARQ) , and then the frame losses information is sent to APP layer for proper reference picture selection (RPS). By exploiting the two-level feedback, the methods of rate control and RPS are combined to achieve channel-adaptive video coding. Experimental results show that: compared to the existed scheme without the multilevel feedback, the proposed method can get a significant improvement in Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) for the wireless video transmission.

articleTitle: Embedded OpenFlow MPLS - Based Advance OpenFlow Inter-Domain Communication Proposal
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: As one of most promising and exciting future internet technology OpenFlow is attracting more and more researchers. However the methods and proposal of the inter-domain communication is still a key problem. In this paper, a EOF-MPLS methods is proposed to solve this problem. In this new technology, OpenFlow controller is responsible for the generation of the FEC and label binding algorithm. Users can use the operation system API provided by the OpenFlow controller to customize the details about the FEC and LDP, thus generate the FEC combined with labels. Considering the message reaching the boundary, Boundary OpenFlow Switch is responsible for identifying and forwarding packets to the other AS and it will complete the label replacement. The boundary OpenFlow is quite important that it should identify multiple protocols from different ASs, even some AS that has different internet structure such as NDN network structure. RSVP and traffic engineering can also be added to the process of FEC generation operated by the OpenFlow Controller. As a consequence, an entropy is used to evaluate the various affecting factors about the EOF-MPLS to the OpenFlow. Calculate the B-indicator to the A-indicator and the A-indicator to the total target one. The result shows that the most complicated A-indicator is the FEC and label combining while the most complicated B-indicator is the label number and TOS.

articleTitle: Balance-Aware Energy-Efficient Geographic Routing for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Geographic routing is an attractive localized routing scheme for wireless sensor networks (WSNs). Most WSNs are consisted of nodes which are all limited in power, so how to employ a proper routing protocol to save energy consumption is a hot topic for research. In this paper, a balance-aware energy-efficient geographic routing protocol BEGR is proposed. Both energy consumption in communication and residual energy at nodes are considered in BEGR. We prove that our protocol is loop-free and can adapt to dynamic scenarios. Simulation results demonstrate that BEGR is better than other protocols in prolonging network lifetime greatly based on first-dead time.

articleTitle: Power and Bandwidth Efficient Q-Ary LDPC Coded Partial Response Continuous Phase Modulation
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Continuous Phase Modulation (CPM) provides an attractive option for spectral efficient communication systems. Binary low-density parity-check (LDPC) coded CPM can improve power efficiency and attain high error correcting capacity, but the convergence of threshold is still much higher than Shannon limit. In order to improve bit error performance, bandwidth efficiency and reduction of convergence threshold compared to above-mentioned scheme, we employ LDPC codes over GF(q>2) as the outer code. In this paper, the combination of q-ary LDPC coding and partial response CPM (PRCPM) is presented, then the effect of LDPC code length, code rate and iterative number on the performance of the system is studied. In the proposed scheme, q-ary LDPC codes and PRCPM are considered together to improve both error performance and bandwidth efficiencies, and the combination can achieve better trade-off between power efficiency and bandwidth efficiency than binary LDPC coded CPM. Meanwhile, the LDPC codes over GF(q) combined with q-ary CPM can avoid the conversion from bit probability to symbol probability and its inversion in combination of binary LDPC coded q-ary CPM, and improve reliability of information transmission.

articleTitle: A Novel Low Complexity Cell Search Algorithm for TD-LTE Advanced System
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Initial cell search synchronization in the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Long Term Evolution (LTE) system includes the time synchronization, the frequency synchronization of frames and the acquisition of cell identity (Cell ID). How to efficiently compensate initial frequency offset, combat uplink interference and adjust the automatic gain control (AGC) in initial cell search procedure will dominate heavily the TIE cell search performance. In the conventional algorithm, it can be achieved by exploiting the essential near-perfect auto coherent detector and cross-correlation. For TD-LTE advanced system, we make good use of the character which the distance between PSS and SSS for TD-LTE is larger than FDD mode. We present a novel, low complexity, robust cell search for TD-LTE advanced system. The algorithm and scheme uses a non-coherent approach to calculate the initial frequency offset, meanwhile by exploiting the property of Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequences that the detected peak timing is shifted under frequency offset, the PSS detection will always will be discovered regardless of the frequency offset in practice of cell search procedure. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme is more robust, less complexity and effective than conventional approaches in TDLTE advanced system.

articleTitle: Error Concealment Algorithms and Quality Evaluation for H.264 Videos
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: During transmission, compressed video streams of H.264/AVC are very likely to be corrupted by channel distortion. In order to resolve the problem, researchers come out with a solution called error concealment which is done at the decoder side. In this paper we conduct a research on BMA and the motion compensated error concealment methods. Compared with BMA, the MCEC algorithm is capable of providing better performance considering various packet loss rates. And the experiment results show that the objective scores of quality are consistent with the perceptual quality.

articleTitle: Call Blocking Probability and Packet Delay in Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In a cognitive radio network (CRN), an preempted secondary user (SU) is placed in a call level queue to wait for accessing another channel. If the availability of channels is transparent to SUs, packets will be generated during their waiting time and the performance of the CRN will be influenced by which way to handle these packets. In this paper, an analytical model for both call-level and packet-level performance evaluation for SUs in cognitive radio networks is developed. The call level performance measure (i.e. call blocking probability) and the packet level performance measure (i.e. packet delay) can be obtained from the analytical model. Numerical results show that analytical model is consistent with simulation results.

articleTitle: Coded Cooperation with Permutation and Block Encoding for Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: A novel coded cooperation scheme based on the intersection of interleaved block codes is proposed for multisource multi-relay networks. Specifically, the multiple source data are jointly encoded and forwarded to the destination by multiple cooperative relays while the sources and relays have low complexity. In this way, a distributed coding scheme with permutation and block encoding is constructed to achieve diversity and coding gains simultaneously. The scheme can achieve significant performance gain over direct transmission and fit for cooperative networks with different number of sources or relays.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Frame Synchronization in Burst OFDM Communication Based on IEEE802.11a
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Synchronization is a very important issue in communication systems. In this paper, it presents the implementation of the frame synchronization in burst Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplex (OFDM) communication based on Std IEEE 802.11a. The algorithm of frame synchronization is on the base of the classic Schmidl-Cox algorithm and detects a certain sample length. It can avoid the impact of the larger random noise, compared to the traditional packet detection algorithm. The frame synchronization is realized by the use of ten repeated short training symbols to determine the starting position of the data packet. Furthermore, the entire frame synchronization is implemented by Xilinx Field-Programmable Gate Array(FPGA) Virtex2 device.

articleTitle: Design of UHF-Band Conformal Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we present a UHF-band compact conformal dipole antenna. Firstly, a planar dipole antenna is designed. And several parameters of the planar dipole antenna structure are discussed in detail. Secondly, the conformal dipole antenna mounted on the cylindrical body is simulated. Finally, the small conformal dipole antenna is fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: Saturation Throughput Analysis of IEEE 802.11b DCF Considering Capture Effects
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we provides a simple and accurate analysis by Markov chain modeling to evaluate the IEEE 802.11 DCF performance in the presence of capture effect. We extend the Bianchi's multidimensional Markov chain analytical model of IEE 802.11 DCF to characterize the behavior of DCF considering capture effect and packet retransmission limits. We compare the NS-2 simulation results with the derived analysis. Numerical results and simulations are provided to validate the accuracy of our model.

articleTitle: Detection and Identification of EM Field Source by Using Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: An approach of tempest analysis is introduced and a method of detection and identification of electromagnetic emitting systems by intentionally or unintentionally is applied and discussed. Based on Support Vector Machine(SVM) algorithm, digital signal process method, this paper investigates an primary procedure involving red/black separation and classifying the emission sources radiated from electronics equipments such as the PCB layout or others. The transmission of digital clock and oscillation in ARM embedded system including tracks configuration and I/O Ports is taken into consideration. A set of computed spectra data of emission caused by PCB is adopted for the learning process. A simplify method to train the SVM is used by extracting the characters like the mean of magnitude, standard deviation and other parameters extracted from the data.

articleTitle: An Improved Wireless Broadcasting Retransmission Approach Based on Network Coding
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Based on the retransmission approach in wireless broadcasting based on network coding (NCWBR), which would decline the performance of the network and increase the retransmission numbers if the same node has more than two losing packets, we present an improved version of NCWBR, which can utilize multiple coded packets to decode data packets (Improved NCWBR). Theoretical analysis reveals that this way can ensure the solvability in the received nodes, and have the lower retransmission numbers. Simulation results indicate that compared with NCWBR approach, the approach presented in this paper can effectively reduce the retransmission numbers and improve the efficiency of transmission.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Network Simulation Testbed Based on Network Virtualization
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Network Virtualization is currently considered as one of the most important approaches to the development of future Internet architecture. In addition to paperwork, most related works also need to be evaluated and verified through testbed. Some large- scale research network test platforms are designed. But they are not suitable for researchers to carry out small-scale network virtualization experiments, because they are quite complexity or still at primary stages. Taking use of Click Modular Router, this paper proposes a future Internet testbed architecture based on network virtualization, supporting the reconfiguration of IPv4 and IPv6 protocols. Experimental results of multi-protocols and multicast applications show that the future Internet testbed proposed in the paper is efficient for future Internet experiments.

articleTitle: Reliable and Efficient Data Dissemination Protocol in VANETs
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
abstract: Data dissemination in vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) has recently received considerable attention. Due to the unique characteristics of VANET, the implementation of reliable data dissemination among vehicles has encountered many challenges. In this paper, a reliable and efficient data dissemination scheme is presented. Relative locations between neighbor vehicles are predicted to improve delivery reliability. Based on assisted nodes which could customize the amount of data according to drivers' different requirements, the novel scheme increases the network connectivity while reducing redundant network traffic. Simulation results show that our novel scheme can obviously improve the network performance in terms of data dissemination rate and data dissemination delay.

articleTitle: Mimicry Honeypot: A Brief Introduction
publicationTitle: 2012 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing
